Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Mas: These are among the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah, the separated letters that open some surahs), and they are read thus: alif, lam, mim, sad. God knows best what He intends by them.

Kitab: That is, this is a Book.

Haraj: Constriction, tightness.

Dhikra: A reminder by which they remember God and what He has, and what is with Him, so that they turn devotedly to His obedience.

Awliya': Their leaders in polytheism.

Wa-ma tadhakkarun: That is, you take heed and so return to the truth.

Wa-kam min qaryah: That is, many towns.

Ba'sana bayatan: Our punishment by night while they are asleep.

Aw hum qa'ilun: That is, sleeping at midday rest, being at ease.

Fa-ma kana da'wahum: That is, their supplication, except their saying, "Indeed we were wrongdoers."

Meaning of the verses:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad.﴾ These letters point to the fact that this Qur'an is composed of letters like these disjointed letters, and you have been unable to produce its like. Thereby it becomes evident that it is the speech of God and His revelation to His Messenger, so believe in it. His words ﴿A Book﴾ mean: this is a Book ﴿revealed to you﴾, O our Messenger, ﴿so let there be no constriction in your breast because of it﴾, that is, no tightness from it, ﴿that you may warn thereby﴾ your people of the consequences of their polytheism and misguidance, and remind the believers among them with it as a reminder. And say to them: ﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ of guidance and light, ﴿and do not follow other than Him﴾, that is, other than Him, ﴿as protectors﴾ who will not command you except to polytheism, evil and corruption, and they are the leaders of error among Quraysh. ﴿Little do you take heed﴾, that is, you take heed so as to return to the truth from which you have turned aside. ﴿And how many a town﴾, that is, and many towns, whose people We destroyed because they turned away from the truth and clung to falsehood. ﴿Our punishment came upon them﴾, that is, Our severe punishment, ﴿by night or while they were resting at midday﴾, that is, by night or by day. Their supplication at that time was only their saying: "Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers." So they acknowledged their sin, but it was far too late for confession to benefit them after witnessing the punishment.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The Noble Qur'an is the source of the Messenger's (ﷺ) warning and good tidings, through what it contains of promise and threat, reminder and glad tidings.

2- The obligation to follow revelation, and the prohibition of following what those driven by desires and innovators call to.

3- Taking heed from what befell the wrongdoing nations of ruin and destruction.

4- Repentance does not benefit at the moment of witnessing death or punishment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 6–10:

Explanation of the words:

"Arsala ilayhim" (He sent to them): they are the nations and peoples.

"Falanaqussanna 'alayhim bi-'ilm" (We will surely relate to them with knowledge): We will inform them of their deeds, following them up, leaving nothing out of them.

"Wa ma kunna ghaa'ibin" (And We were not absent): that is, not absent from them during the days they were acting.

"Al-wazn yawma'idhin al-haqq" (The weighing that Day is the truth): that is, the justice.

"Faman thaqulat mawazinuhu" (As for those whose scales are heavy): that is, with good deeds; "fa-ulaa'ika hum al-muflihun" (those are the ones who will prosper) by entering Paradise.

"Khasiru anfusahum" (They have lost themselves): by entering the Fire and burning in it forever.

"Ma'ayish" (means of livelihood): plural of "ma'ishah", meaning the living that a person lives.

"Qaleelan ma tashkurun" (Little are you grateful): that is, little gratitude. Gratitude (shukr) is acknowledging the blessing to its Benefactor, obeying Him by doing what He loves and abstaining from what He dislikes.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. And We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.﴾ The Exalted informs that when He gathers the creation for the judgment of the decision, affirming the report with an oath, He will question every nation, community or individual to whom He sent His messengers, asking them about the extent to which they responded to their messengers' call: whether they believed in what the messengers brought them and obeyed them in what they conveyed to them, of monotheism, worship, obedience and submission. Likewise the messengers will be questioned: whether they conveyed what they were entrusted with of His message, which includes commanding His servants to believe in Him, to affirm His oneness and to obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. Then the Exalted will relate to all of them, with His knowledge, everything that came from them of outward and inward deeds, and they will not be able to hide anything at all. His questioning them at first was only for the sake of establishing the proof, manifesting His justice, may He be glorified and exalted, concerning them, and for rebuking whoever among them deserves rebuke. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾ from them while they were working in the world; all their deeds were exposed and manifest to Him, the Exalted, and nothing of them is hidden from Him, for He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

This is what the first verse [6] and the second [7] indicate. As for the third and fourth verses, the Exalted informs that after questioning them and making them aware of their deeds, the scale will be set up and their deeds will be weighed for them. Whoever's good deeds are heavy in the scale will prosper, by being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise, the Abode of Peace. And whoever's scale is light, due to few good deeds and many evil deeds, has lost himself by being cast into Hell to abide in everlasting punishment. The Exalted gave the reason for this loss in Hell with His words: ﴿because they were wronging Our signs﴾, that is, they denied and rejected them. "Zulm" (wrongdoing) is used here while "takdhib" (denial) and "juhud" (rejection) are intended, for two reasons:

First: the preposition "bi" (with/by) suffices, since "zulm" is not construed with it; rather it is "kadhaba bihi" (he denied it) or "jahada bihi" (he rejected it), and one does not say "zalama bihi" but "zalamahu". This is by way of "tadmin" (implicit meaning), which is permissible in the Arabic language in which the Qur'an was revealed.

Second: instead of believing in the signs, which were clear, they denied them, so it was as if they had wronged the signs with a wrong, in that they did not believe in them, though they were manifest.

This is what the two verses indicate. As for the fifth verse [10], it contains the favour of God the Exalted upon His servants. It was required that they thank His blessings upon them by believing in Him, affirming His oneness and obeying Him, but what occurred was the lack of gratitude from most of them. The Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly established you upon the earth﴾, where He made them firmly established in life upon it, managing its affairs and walking in its tracts. His words ﴿and made for you therein means of livelihood﴾ are another blessing: that He made for them in it means of livelihood and provisions which they seek and obtain, and upon which their lives are sustained. His words ﴿little are you grateful﴾ mean: you give thanks only with a small gratitude, hardly worth mentioning.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the creed of resurrection, questioning, reckoning and the weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

2- The severity of the situation, as nations and messengers, peace be upon them, are all questioned alike.

3- Success and loss are based on what one earns in this world: whoever earns good is saved, and whoever earns evil is destroyed.

4- The obligation to thank blessings through faith and obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verse 11–18:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Khalaqnakum thumma sawwarnakum﴾: That is, We created your father Adam, meaning We determined him from clay, then We fashioned him in the noble human form, which his descendants inherited after him until the end of human existence.

﴿Fa-sajadu﴾: That is, a prostration of greeting to Adam, peace be upon him.

Iblis: the father of the jinn devils, whose kunya (teknonym) is Abu Murrah, and he is the accursed Shaytan.

﴿Fa-hbit minha﴾: That is, from the Garden.

﴿Min al-saghirin﴾: plural of saghir, the humiliated and disgraced.

﴿Fa-bima aghwaytani﴾: That is, because of your misguiding me.

﴿Madhmuman madhhuran﴾: detested, blamed, and expelled.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with enumerating the blessings of God the Exalted upon His servants, blessings that require gratitude to Him through faith in Him and obedience. God the Exalted says: ﴿And We did certainly create you and then give you form﴾: that is, We created your father Adam from clay, then We fashioned him in the human form which his descendants inherited from him. ﴿Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾: and in this is another blessing, which is the honouring of your father Adam by commanding the angels to prostrate to him as a greeting and in veneration of him. ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated﴾: that is, he refused and declined to prostrate. So his Lord, the Exalted, asked him, saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾: that is, what made you not prostrate? Iblis answered, saying: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾: meaning, I am more noble than him, so how could I prostrate to him? Iblis was not correct in this flawed analogy. Firstly: fire is not nobler than clay; rather clay is more beneficial and less harmful, while fire is entirely harm, and whatever benefit is in it is nothing alongside its harm. Secondly: the one who commanded him to prostrate is the Lord whose obedience is obligatory, whether the one prostrated to is superior or inferior. Here the Lord the Exalted commanded him to descend from the Garden, so He said: ﴿So descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the humiliated﴾: that is, the abased and despised. When Iblis fell into his predicament, and knew the cause of his ruin, which was his not prostrating to Adam, he said to the Lord, blessed and exalted: ﴿Reprieve me﴾: that is, give me respite, do not cause me to die, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾. The Lord answered him with His saying: ﴿Until the Day of the Time Appointed﴾ [al-Hijr: 38], which is the end of this world only, and that is before the resurrection. This answer came in Surat al-Hijr, and here He said: ﴿Indeed, you are of those reprieved﴾. Iblis's intention in the respite was to be able to corrupt the greatest number of the children of Adam, as vengeance against them, since Adam was the cause of his expulsion from mercy. When the Lord granted his request, he said: ﴿Because You have sent me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾: he means Adam and his descendants, and by the straight path is meant Islam, since it is the straight way that leads its traveller to the pleasure of God the Exalted. ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and on their right and on their left﴾: he means he will surround them, preventing them from following the straight path so that they do not escape and perish as he himself perished, may God increase his perdition. His saying ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾ is Iblis's statement to the Lord, the Exalted: you will not find most of the children of Adam, on whose account You have misguided me, thankful to You through faith, monotheism and acts of obedience.

Here God renewed His command to expel the accursed one, saying: ﴿Get out of it﴾: that is, from the Garden, ﴿disgraced and expelled﴾: that is, detested and driven away, ﴿Whoever follows you of them, I will surely fill Hell with you all together﴾: that is, by My might, I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever of them follows you, all together.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The danger of arrogance for a person.

2- The harm of flawed analogy.

3- The danger of Iblis and his offspring to the children of Adam, and deliverance from them through the remembrance of God the Exalted and gratitude to Him.

4- Gratitude is faith and obedience to God and His Messenger ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 19–22:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-zawjuka (and your spouse): this is Hawwa' (Eve), whom Allah the Exalted created from the left rib of Adam.

Al-Jannah (the Garden): the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey) and the Mi'raj (Ascension).

Min al-zalimin (among the wrongdoers): that is, to their own selves.

Fa-waswasa (then he whispered): al-waswasa is a hidden sound. The whispering of Satan to the son of Adam is the casting into his chest of corrupt and harmful meanings, made attractive so that he believes in them, speaks by them, or acts upon them.

Li-yubdiya lahuma ma wuriya (to reveal to them what was concealed): to make apparent to them what was hidden from them of their private parts ('awrat).

Wa-qasamahuma (and he swore to them): he swore to each of them.

Fa-dallahuma bi-ghurur (so he brought them down by deception): that is, he lowered them little by little, by his trickery and deceit, until they both ate from the tree.

Wa-tafiqa yakhsifan (and they began to fasten upon themselves): they began to bind over themselves leaves of the Garden in order to cover their private parts.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Most Merciful expelled Iblis from the Garden, He called out to Adam, saying to him: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your spouse﴾, that is Hawwa', ﴿in the Garden, and eat from wherever you wish﴾, meaning from its fruits and bounties, ﴿but do not approach this tree﴾. He pointed out to them a specific tree among the trees of the Garden, forbade them from eating of it, and informed them that if they ate of it they would be among the wrongdoers deserving punishment. Iblis seized this opportunity that had been granted to him, and whispered to them, making eating from the tree seem attractive to them, saying to them: ﴿Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels or become of the immortals﴾. ﴿And he swore to them﴾, that is, he swore to them that he was sincerely advising them and was not deceiving them. ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾ and trickery until they ate. ﴿Then when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them﴾, that is, their nakedness appeared to them when the light that had covered them was removed, so they began to bind leaves of the Garden upon themselves to cover their private parts. This is the meaning of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they began to fasten upon themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾. At that moment their Lord, glorified and exalted, called out to them saying: Did I not forbid you from this tree? This is a rhetorical question of discipline and reproach. ﴿And I said to you: Indeed Satan is to you a clear enemy﴾. How then did you accept his advice when he is your enemy?

Guidance from the verses:

1. The weapon with which Iblis fights the son of Adam is whispering and beautifying (falsehood), and nothing else.

2. Affirmation of Satan's enmity toward man.

3. A prohibition implies prohibition (haram), unless there is an indication that turns it toward disapproval (karahah).

4. The obligation to cover the 'awrah, for men and women alike.

5. The permissibility of swearing by Allah the Exalted, but one should swear only truthfully.

4. The obligation to cover the 'awrah, for men and women alike.

5. The permissibility of swearing by Allah the Exalted, but one should swear only truthfully.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 19–22:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-zawjuka (and your spouse): this is Hawwa' (Eve), whom Allah the Exalted created from the left rib of Adam.

Al-Jannah (the Garden): the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam), which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey) and the Mi'raj (Ascension).

Min al-zalimin (among the wrongdoers): that is, to their own selves.

Fa-waswasa (then he whispered): al-waswasa is a hidden sound. The whispering of Satan to the son of Adam is the casting into his chest of corrupt and harmful meanings, made attractive so that he believes in them, speaks by them, or acts upon them.

Li-yubdiya lahuma ma wuriya (to reveal to them what was concealed): to make apparent to them what was hidden from them of their private parts ('awrat).

Wa-qasamahuma (and he swore to them): he swore to each of them.

Fa-dallahuma bi-ghurur (so he brought them down by deception): that is, he lowered them little by little, by his trickery and deceit, until they both ate from the tree.

Wa-tafiqa yakhsifan (and they began to fasten upon themselves): they began to bind over themselves leaves of the Garden in order to cover their private parts.

When the Most Merciful expelled Iblis from the Garden, He called out to Adam, saying to him: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your spouse﴾, that is Hawwa', ﴿in the Garden, and eat from wherever you wish﴾, meaning from its fruits and bounties, ﴿but do not approach this tree﴾. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 23–25:

Explanation of the words:

"Zalamna anfusana" (We have wronged ourselves): that is, by their eating from the tree.

"Al-Khasirin" (the losers): those who lost entry into Paradise and living in it.

"Mustaqarr" (a dwelling): a place of settling and residence.

"Mata' ila hin" (enjoyment until a term): enjoyment of life until the end of your appointed times.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns Adam, peace be upon him. When Adam and Hawwa' tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and their Lord rebuked them for that. They said, declaring their repentance: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers﴾, meaning, among the ruined. They repented, and God the Exalted accepted their repentance and said to them: "Descend to the earth," since Paradise, which is in the heaven, was no longer a dwelling for them after committing the disobedience. Iblis disobeyed by refusing to prostrate to Adam, and Adam and Hawwa' by eating from the tree. His saying ﴿Some of you are enemies to others﴾ means: descend to the earth while some of you are enemies to others. Iblis and his offspring are enemies to Adam and his children, and Adam and his children are enemies to Iblis and his offspring. ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾ means a place of settlement, ﴿and provision for a time﴾ means enjoyment of life until the end of the appointed times. His exalted saying ﴿Therein you will live, therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth﴾ refers to the earth to which they were sent down, which is this earth on which the children of Adam live. By "being brought forth" is meant coming out of the graves to the resurrection and the gathering.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The saying of Adam and Hawwa': ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves...﴾ is the word which God cast to Adam, whereby he received it and He accepted his repentance.

2- A condition of repentance is acknowledging the sin, which is done through seeking forgiveness, that is, asking for pardon.

3- The ill consequence of sin was the cause of Iblis's expulsion from mercy and of Adam's removal from Paradise.

4- A human life is not completed anywhere other than on earth, nor is one buried after death in anything other than it, as indicated by the verse ﴿Therein you will live, therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth﴾.

Explanation of the key words:

Wariisha (ريشاً): clothing of adornment and need.

Yuwari saw'atakum (يواري سوءاتكم): covers your private parts.

Libas al-taqwa (لباس التقوى): better in preserving the private parts, the bodies, the minds and the morals.

Min ayat Allah (من آيات الله): among the signs of His power.

La yaftinannakum (لا يفتننكم): that they not turn you away from obedience to God, which brings about His pleasure and companionship in the highest dominion.

Abawaykum (أبويكم): Adam and Hawwa' (Eve).

Qabiluhu (قبيله): his hosts, his troops from the jinn.

Fahisha (فاحشة): an ugly trait of extreme ugliness, such as circumambulating the House naked.

The meanings of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as adornment﴾. This noble address is intended as a reminder to the polytheists of Quraysh of God's blessings and His power over them, so that perhaps they will remember, believe and submit by abandoning polytheism and sins. Among His blessings upon them is that He sent down to them clothing with which they cover their private parts. ﴿Riyash﴾ is clothing with which they beautify themselves, at their festivals and occasions. Then God, exalted is He, informed that the garment of piety is better for its wearer than the garment of cloth, because the pious person is a servant committed to obeying God and His Messenger, and God and His Messenger command the covering of private parts, the warding off of harms, and the preservation of dignity, and they command modesty, chastity, good bearing, and cleanliness of body and clothing. So where is the garment of cloth, stripped of piety, from these??

His saying, ﴿That is among the signs of God﴾, meaning, among the evidences of His power that necessitate belief in Him and obedience to Him. His saying ﴿that perhaps they may remember﴾ means in hope that they will recall these blessings and give thanks through belief and obedience.

This is what the first verse [26] indicates. In the second verse [27] He addressed them a second time, saying, ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping off their clothing to show them their private parts﴾. He warns them against the seduction of Satan, reminding them of what he did to their two parents, namely removing them from Paradise after stripping off their clothing, so that their private parts were exposed, which caused their expulsion from the abode of peace, alerting them to the danger of the enemy, since he sees them, he and his troops, while they do not see them. Then God, exalted is He, informed that He made the devils allies of those who do not believe, in accordance with His practice in His creation. The devils embody the summit of evil and wickedness, and those who do not believe have hearts darkened by the absence of the light of faith within them, so they are prepared to accept the devils and to accept what they whisper and inspire of various kinds of corruption and evils, such as polytheism and sins of all kinds. Thus the alliance between the devils and the disbelievers is complete. As proof of this alliance between them, when the polytheists commit a fahisha, a despicable trait of extreme ugliness, and are forbidden from it, they justify their act by claiming that they found their fathers doing it and that God commanded them to do it. This is a false argument, for the following reasons:

First: the deeds of their fathers are neither religion nor law.

Second: God, the Wise, the All-Knowing, is far above commanding indecency; it is only those who commit indecencies, namely the devils and their human allies, who command it. Therefore God answered them with His saying ﴿Indeed, God does not command indecency﴾, and rebuked them, reproaching them with His saying: ﴿Do you say about God what you do not know?﴾

Guidance of the verses

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The reminder of God's blessings, which calls for thanks through faith and piety.

2- Warning against Satan and his temptation, especially since he sees the human while the human does not see him.

3- Disbelieving hearts are the sinful ones, and thus the alliance between the devils and the disbelievers is complete.

4- The ugliness and prohibition of indecencies.

5- The invalidity of justifying an act by people's practice, since there is no proof except divine revelation.

6- God, exalted is He, is far above approving of indecencies, let alone commanding them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 29–31:

Explanation of the words:

Al-qist (al-qist): justice in speech, judgment and action.

Aqimu wujuhakum (أقيموا وجوهكم): i.e., devote your worship sincerely to Allah and face His House.

Kama bada'akum ta'udun (كما بدأكم تعودون): as He originated your creation the first time, He will restore you after death, alive.

Awliya' min dun Allah (أولياء من دون الله): those whom they take as allies out of love, support and obedience, apart from Allah the Exalted.

Zinatakum (زينتكم): i.e., wear your clothing when entering the prayer.

Wa la tusrifu (ولا تسرفوا): in eating or drinking; al-israf (excess, al-israf) is exceeding the required limit in everything.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues to explain the errors of the polytheists of Quraysh, for in the previous verses they argued, in justification of their immoral acts, that they had found their fathers doing so and that Allah had commanded them to do it. Allah refuted them in this. In this verse [29] Allah says: ﴿Say﴾, O Our Messenger, ﴿"My Lord has commanded justice"﴾, which is justice, namely faith in Allah and His Messenger and the affirmation of Allah's oneness in worship, and it is not polytheism with Allah, the committing of immoral acts, or lying against Allah by claiming that He has made lawful such-and-such when He has not made it lawful, or forbidden such-and-such when He has not forbidden it. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"And set your faces right at every place of prayer"﴾, i.e., say to them, O Our Messenger: set your faces right at every place of prayer, meaning devote your worship sincerely to Allah and face His Sacred House. ﴿"And call upon Him, sincerely devoted to Him in religion"﴾, i.e., call upon Him alone and do not call upon anyone along with Him. His saying: ﴿"As He originated you, so you will return"﴾ reminds them of the Hereafter and the second life, for whoever believes in life after death and in being recompensed for his deeds, whether good or evil, is able to remain upright in justice and goodness throughout his life. His saying ﴿"A party He has guided, and a party upon whom error has been justly decreed"﴾ is an explanation of His justice, His wisdom and the manifestations of His power. He is the Originator, the Restorer, the Guide and the Misleader; to Him belongs absolute dominion and sole rule. How, then, can idols and images be set up as equal to Him? He guided a party of His servants, and they were guided; and He left others astray, and they went astray, but this was due to their aversion to guidance and their alliance with the people of misguidance. ﴿"Indeed, they took the devils as allies rather than Allah"﴾, and so they went far astray. ﴿"And they suppose"﴾, because of their deep immersion in darkness and error, ﴿"that they are guided"﴾.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer"﴾, i.e., wear your clothing when circling the House, so that you do not circumambulate naked, and when praying, so that you do not pray with your private parts uncovered as the polytheists do, who take the devils as allies; they were led astray until immoral acts were made attractive to them in word, deed and belief. His saying: ﴿"And eat and drink, but do not be excessive"﴾, i.e., eat of what Allah has made lawful for you and drink, and do not be excessive by forbidding what Allah has made lawful or by legislating what He has not prescribed for you. So adhere to justice, for He, the Exalted, does not love the excessive; so seek His love through justice, and avoid His displeasure by obeying Him and His Messenger ﷺ.

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of justice in speech and in judgment.

2- The obligation of sincerity in worship, whether prayer or supplication, to Allah the Exalted.

3- The affirmation of divine decree (al-qadar).

4- The obligation of covering the private parts in prayer.

5- The prohibition of excess in eating and drinking, and in everything.

The context continues to explain the errors of the polytheists of Quraysh, for in the previous verses they argued, in justification of their immoral acts, that they had found their fathers doing so and that Allah had commanded them to do it. Allah refuted them in this. In this verse [29] Allah says: ﴿Say﴾, O Our Messenger, ﴿"My Lord has commanded justice"﴾, which is justice, namely faith in Allah and His Messenger and the affirmation of Allah's oneness in worship, and it is not polytheism with Allah, the committing of immoral acts, or lying against Allah by claiming that He has made lawful such-and-such when He has not made it lawful, or forbidden such-and-such when He has not forbidden it. 2- The obligation of sincerity in worship, whether prayer or supplication, to Allah the Exalted.

3- The affirmation of divine decree (al-qadar).

4- The obligation of covering the private parts in prayer.

5- The prohibition of excess in eating and drinking, and in everything.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Man harrama zinatallah* (who has forbidden the adornment of God): *al-tahrim* means prohibition, and *al-zina* means that with which one adorns oneself, such as clothing and other things.

*Al-tayyibat* (the good things): the plural of *tayyib*, which means lawful and not repugnant.

*Khalisatan* (exclusively): not shared with the disbelievers, because they are in the Fire.

*Al-fawahish* (indecencies): the plural of *fahisha*, here meaning fornication and sodomy, whether committed in secret or openly.

*Al-ithm* (sin): everything harmful and ugly, including wine and other sins.

*Al-baghy bi-ghayr al-haqq* (oppression without right): injustice without retaliation or punishment in kind.

*Wa an tushriku* (and that you associate partners): that is, *shirk* with God, which is worshipping other than God, the Exalted.

*Al-sultan* (authority): the proof by which disputed or contested rights are established.

*Ajal* (term): a fixed time at which something ends.

**The meaning of the verses:**

When the polytheists forbade circumambulating the House in clothing and circumambulated it naked, claiming that they do not circumambulate in garments in which they have disobeyed God, God, the Exalted, denounced this, saying: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾, such as the flesh of what they had forbidden of the *sawa'ib* (free-roaming animals). So the interrogative in His words ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God﴾ is for denunciation. The meaning of "brought forth" is that He brought forth vegetation from the earth, such as cotton and flax, and iron ores, since coats of mail are made of iron. His words ﴿It is for those who believed in the life of this world﴾ mean primarily, because the believers are knowledgeable, so they perform good work, production and craftsmanship well, while the disbelievers follow them in this due to their ignorance, laziness and lack of insight. ﴿Exclusively on the Day of Resurrection﴾ means that it is exclusively for the believers on the Day of Resurrection, with no disbelievers sharing it with them, and because the disbelievers are in the abode of misery, the Fire, we seek refuge in God, the Exalted. His words ﴿Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know﴾ mean: like this detailed and clarified explanation which We have made clear and distinguished in these verses, and We continue to detail and clarify what We send down of the verses of the noble Qur'an, for a people who know. As for others, the people of ignorance and error, they do not benefit from it, because they are veiled by the darkness of disbelief and polytheism and the smoke of desires, lusts and doubts.

This is what the first verse [32] indicates. As for the second verse [33], it contains a statement of the principal prohibited matters and the chief sins, which are: indecencies, whether apparent or hidden; sin (*ithm*), which is all other disobediences, whether by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibition; and transgression (*baghy*), which is domineering over people and attacking them by violating their rights, taking their wealth and harming their bodies, without a right that necessitates and justifies that attack, such as when a person attacks and is then retaliated against and punished with the like of what he committed and wronged; also *shirk* with God by worshipping other than Him; and saying about God without knowledge from Him, such as legislating what He has not legislated, forbidding what He has not forbidden, and obligating what He has not obligated.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of the verses:

1. Strong denunciation of those who forbid what God has made lawful of the good things, like some extremists.

2. Pleasant foods and drinks, and adornments of clothing and other things, are more fitting for believers than others, because they perform good work and exert effort to extract them and benefit from them. Unlike people of ignorance, who are blind and cannot see, and paralysed and cannot move. If it is said that the opposite is correct, since the nations of disbelief, Europe and America, are those who have advanced industrially and enjoyed what believers have not enjoyed? Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 35–36:

Explanation of the words:

"Immā yaʾtiyannakum" (إما يأتينكم): the origin of "immā" is "in" (إن), the conditional particle, and "mā" is an added particle to strengthen the speech. The "n" of "in" was assimilated into "mā," so it became "immā."

"Yaqussūna ʿalaykum āyātī" (يقصون عليكم آياتي): they will recite My verses to you, verse after verse, explaining to you what they indicate of God's rulings and laws, and His promise and warning.

"Famani ittaqā" (فمن اتقى): that is, from polytheism (shirk), so he did not associate partners with God, and he reformed himself through righteous deeds.

"Falā khawfun ʿalayhim" (فلا خوف عليهم): in this world and the Hereafter.

"Walā hum yaḥzanūn" (ولا هم يحزنون): over what they left behind, or what they missed obtaining of the affairs of this world.

The meaning of the two verses:

This call may be a general address to all of Adam's children, as is the apparent sense of the wording, and that all of humanity was addressed with it through the tongues of their messengers. It may also be specific to the polytheists of the Arabs, and the intended messenger would be Muhammad ﷺ, mentioned in the plural form as a sign of honor and dignity for him. What humanity, or the polytheists of the Arabs, were addressed with is God the Exalted's information to them that whoever is reached by a messenger from his own kind, reciting to him the verses of his Lord, which carry knowledge of God, His attributes, and an explanation of what He loves and what He hates, then whoever fears God by abandoning polytheism toward Him, and reforms what he had corrupted before knowledge, of his soul, his character and his mind, through faith and righteous deeds, these are in God's judgment: "there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve" (﴿فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ولا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾) in both lives. As for those who denied the verses of God that the messengers brought and related to them, and who were arrogant about acting upon them just as they were arrogant about believing in them, these are the ones far removed from every good, "the companions of the Fire" (﴿أصْحَٰبُ ٱلنّارِ﴾), meaning its people, "they will abide therein forever" (﴿هُمْ فِيها خَٰلِدُونَ﴾), never leaving it under any circumstances.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Cutting off the argument of the children of Adam by sending messengers to them.

2- The first thing one begins with in the matter of piety is abandoning shirk, so that the believing person first clears himself of it.

3- Reform comes through righteous deeds that God has prescribed, which purify souls and cleanse them.

4- Denial and arrogance are both barriers to piety and righteous deeds, and therefore their companions are the companions of the Fire.

What humanity, or the polytheists of the Arabs, were addressed with is God the Exalted's information to them that whoever is reached by a messenger from his own kind, reciting to him the verses of his Lord, which carry knowledge of God, His attributes, and an explanation of what He loves and what He hates, then whoever fears God by abandoning polytheism toward Him, and reforms what he had corrupted before knowledge, of his soul, his character and his mind, through faith and righteous deeds, these are in God's judgment: "there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve" (﴿فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ولا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾) in both lives. As for those who denied the verses of God that the messengers brought and related to them, and who were arrogant about acting upon them just as they were arrogant about believing in them, these are the ones far removed from every good, "the companions of the Fire" (﴿أصْحَٰبُ ٱلنّارِ﴾), meaning its people, "they will abide therein forever" (﴿هُمْ فِيها خَٰلِدُونَ﴾), never leaving it under any circumstances.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Cutting off the argument of the children of Adam by sending messengers to them.

2- The first thing one begins with in the matter of piety is abandoning shirk, so that the believing person first clears himself of it.

3- Reform comes through righteous deeds that God has prescribed, which purify souls and cleanse them.

4- Denial and arrogance are both barriers to piety and righteous deeds, and therefore their companions are the companions of the Fire.

Rusulunā (رسلنا): what is meant by them is the Angel of Death and his helpers.

Ḍallū ʿannā (قالوا ضلوا عنا): they went astray from us, meaning they were absent from us, so we did not see them and did not find them.

Fī umam (في أمم): that is, among a whole multitude of nations.

Ād-dārakū (اداركوا): that is, they overtook one another and joined one another until they all entered it.

Ukhrāhum li-ūlāhum (أخراهم لأولاهم): the followers say to the leaders in misguidance, who are the ones followed.

Taksibūn (تكسبون): from injustice, evil and corruption.

Yaliju al-jamal fī samm al-khiyāṭ (يلج الجمل في سم الخياط): that is, the camel enters the eye of the needle.

Al-mujrimīn (المجرمين): those who commit crimes against themselves, corrupting them through polytheism and sins.

Ghawāshin (غواش): coverings of fire with which they cover themselves likewise.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs that there is no one more unjust, more ignorant, or more astray than he who fabricates lies against God, saying "He has taken a son," or "He has commanded immorality," or "He has forbidden such-and-such" when He has not forbidden it, or who denies His signs which His messengers brought, rejecting them and persisting stubbornly in that and being arrogant. Those fabricators and deniers—God informs that ﴿their share of the Book will reach them﴾, that is, what has been written for them in the Preserved Tablet of good and evil, happiness or misery. ﴿Until, when Our messengers come to them to take them in death﴾, that is, the Angel of Death and his helpers, ﴿they say to them, "Where is that which you used to call upon besides God?"﴾, that is, which allies you used to worship? They answer, saying: ﴿They have gone astray from us﴾, that is, they have disappeared so we do not see them. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾. On the Day of Resurrection it will be said to them: ﴿Enter into nations that passed away before you of jinn and men﴾ into the Fire, and they will enter. ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾. So the polytheists curse one another, and the Jews and Christians likewise. ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾, that is, they have followed one another and their entry into the Fire is complete, they begin to complain: ﴿The last of them will say about the first of them, "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us"﴾, that is, O our Lord, ﴿so give them a double punishment of the Fire﴾, that is, multiplied, ﴿from the Fire.﴾ God answered them by His saying: ﴿For each is double,﴾ meaning each one of you has a double portion of punishment, ﴿but you do not know,﴾ since the abode is an abode of punishment, so it multiplies upon everyone within it. Then ﴿the first of them will say to the last of them, "You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn,"﴾ that is, of polytheism, fabricating against God, denying His signs, and turning away from obeying Him and His Messenger.

This is what the three verses indicate. As for the fourth and fifth verses, the fourth establishes a great ruling, which is that those who denied God's signs and were arrogant toward them, did not believe, did not do righteous deeds, and lived in polytheism, evil and corruption—when one of them dies and the angels ascend with his soul to heaven, the gates of heaven are not opened for him, and his destination is the Fire. As God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾, so He made their entry into Paradise dependent on an impossibility, which is the camel entering the eye of the needle, and whatever is dependent on an impossibility is itself impossible.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus do We recompense the criminals﴾ against themselves, since they corrupted themselves through polytheism and sins. This is what the fourth verse contains, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them—the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.﴾

As for the fifth, it contains the following report: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and over them are coverings﴾, that is, coverings of fire. Just as God, exalted is He, recompenses these deniers, arrogant ones, and criminals, He in His justice recompenses those who wronged themselves, since they defiled and corrupted themselves with the filth of sins and transgressions.

This is what the fourth verse contains, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them—the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.﴾

As for the fifth, it contains the following report: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and over them are coverings﴾, that is, coverings of fire. Just as God, exalted is He, recompenses these deniers, arrogant ones, and criminals, He in His justice recompenses those who wronged themselves, since they defiled and corrupted themselves with the filth of sins and transgressions.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The worst injustice is that which consists of lying against God and denying His laws.

2- Affirmation of the trial of the grave and its punishment.

3- The cursing of the people of the Fire by one another, out of rage against one another, since each one was a cause of the other's punishment.

4- Explanation of the recompense of those who deny God's signs and are arrogant toward them, which is being barred from entering Paradise, and likewise the criminals and wrongdoers.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 42–43:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"إلا وسعها"* (illa wus'aha): its capacity, what it can bear and is able to do of deeds.

*"ونزعنا"* (wa naza'na): i.e., We removed and extracted.

*"من غل"* (min ghill): i.e., from rancor and enmity.

*"هدانا لهذا"* (hadana li-hadha): i.e., to the righteous deed in this world, whose reward is this, namely Paradise.

*"بما كنتم تعملون"* (bi-ma kuntum ta'malun): i.e., because of your righteous deeds, such as prayer, fasting, charity and jihad.

**The meaning of the two verses:**

When the Most High mentioned the reward of those who denied and were arrogant toward faith and righteous deeds, and that reward was wretchedness and deprivation, He mentioned the reward of the people of faith and righteous deeds, saying: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. And since deeds include what is arduous and unbearable and what is easy and within one's ability, He said: ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, i.e., what it is able to do of deeds and what is within its power. Then He informed about the believers who do righteous deeds, saying: ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide eternally﴾.

In the second verse, He informed that He purified them inwardly, removing from their breasts any rancor toward one another, and that rivers flow beneath their palaces, and that they said, thankful for the favors of Allah upon them: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this﴾, i.e., to a righteous deed whose reward is this, namely Paradise and its lasting bliss. They affirmed a truth: that their guidance, whose reward is Paradise, they would not have attained had Allah the Most High not guided them. So they said: ﴿And we would not have been [rightly] guided if Allah had not guided us﴾. Then they said, by Allah: ﴿Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth﴾. So here are the people of disbelief and disobedience in the Fire, and here we are, the people of faith and obedience, in the bliss of Paradise. Thus the messengers were proven true in what they reported of promise and threat. Their Lord, glorified and exalted, called out to them: ﴿That is Paradise, which you have been given as inheritance for what you used to do﴾, whereby their bliss is increased and their happiness is magnified.

**Guidance from the two verses:**

1. Faith and righteous deeds are the two requirements for entering Paradise, bringing honor in both abodes.

2. In the true religion brought by the messengers there is no hardship that cannot be borne, except what is a punishment.

3. There is no enmity or envy in Paradise.

4. Guidance is a gift from Allah, so it is sought from Him alone, and it is not attained except by asking Him, the Most High.

5. The messengers were proven true in what they reported concerning the unseen and other matters.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 44–47:

Explanation of the words:

"Fa-adhdhana mu'adhdhin" (Then a caller called out): i.e., he announced at the top of his voice that the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.

"La'nat Allah" (The curse of God): i.e., He commands that the wrongdoers be expelled from mercy into punishment.

"Yasuddun 'an sabil Allah" (They bar from the way of God): the way of God is Islam, and "sadd" (barring) is turning away; they turned themselves away and turned others away.

"Wa yabghunaha 'iwajan" (And they seek to make it crooked): they seek that the Shari'ah incline with their inclinations and desires, so that it serves their aims.

"Wa baynahuma hijab" (And between them is a veil): i.e., between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell there is a dividing barrier, and it is the wall of al-A'raf.

"Wa 'ala al-A'raf" (And upon the A'raf): a wall between Paradise and Hell. God, Exalted, said in Surat al-Hadid: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a gate﴾ [Verse: 13].

"Ya'rifuna kullan bi-simahum" (They will recognize each by their marks): i.e., each of the people of Paradise and the people of Hell by their signs.

"Suriffat absaruhum" (When their sights are turned): i.e., they looked toward Paradise, where the companions of the Fire are.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of the companions of Paradise and the companions of the Fire. God informs that the companions of Paradise called out to the companions of the Fire, saying to them: "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us of Paradise and its bliss to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you of the Fire and its punishment to be true?" They replied: "Yes, we have indeed found what our Lord promised to be true." At that moment a caller announced: "The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers who bar from the way of God, which is Islam, the path that leads to God's pleasure and Paradise, and who seek to make it crooked, i.e., they want the way of God to be bent so that it turns with them wherever they turn in their evils, corruptions, desires and passions, and they are also disbelievers in the Hereafter." Those [on the A'raf] curse them: "The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers who have these characteristics." God said in the third verse: ﴿And between them﴾, i.e., between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, ﴿is a veil﴾, a dividing barrier, i.e., a barrier, and it is a place on an elevation, upon which are men of the children of Adam whose evil deeds and good deeds are equal; they are detained there until God judges between the people of the assembly, deciding about them, and they enter Paradise, God willing.

As for His saying: ﴿They will recognize each by their marks﴾, i.e., they will recognize the people of Paradise by their marks, which are the whiteness of faces and the radiance of bliss, and they will recognize the people of the Fire by the blackness of faces and the blueness of eyes.

﴿And they call out to the companions of Paradise﴾, i.e., the companions of the A'raf call out to the companions of Paradise, saying: "Peace be upon you," hoping thereby, as God said: ﴿They have not entered it, while they hope [to]﴾. ﴿And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾, i.e., they looked toward the direction of the people of the Fire and saw their faces blackened and their eyes blue, enveloped by punishment from above them and from beneath their feet. They raised their voices saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., the people of the Fire, because they entered it by their wrongdoing. We seek refuge with God.

Guidance from the verses:

1- There is complete connection between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell whenever one of them wishes it, such that if someone in Paradise wants to look at someone in the Fire and speak to him, that is granted to him.

2- It is permissible to apply the word "promise" to "threat" for the sake of parallelism or mockery, as in these verses.

3- Condemnation of barring from the way of God, wrongdoing, and disbelief in the Hereafter, which are causes of misery in the next abode.

4- Establishing the principle that heavy good deeds bring salvation and light ones bring ruin; and whoever's good and evil deeds are equal will be among the last to be saved from entering the Fire.

5- The permissibility of hope when its basis is present.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 48–51:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Bisimahum* (بسيماهم): *al-sima* is the mark that identifies the one who has it.

*Jam'akum* (جمعكم): i.e., your wealth and your men, such as armies.

*A-ha'ula'i* (أهؤلاء): a reference to the weak among the Muslims, who are in Paradise.

*Aw mimma razaqakumu Allah* (أو مما رزقكم الله): i.e., from the food and drink.

*Harramahuma* (حرمهما): prevented them.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The context is still about the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men [from the people of the Fire] whom they recognize by their marks, saying: "Your gathering [of wealth and men] has not availed you, nor has what you used to arrogantly reject"﴾. That is, they recognize them by their marks, which are the marks of the people of the Fire: blackness of faces and blueness of eyes. They call out to them, saying: ﴿"Has your gathering availed you, nor your arrogance"﴾, i.e., your wealth and men for wars and fighting did not avail you, just as your arrogance toward the truth and your disdain for accepting it did not avail you, and now you are in the most severe kinds of punishment. Then they point to the weak among the Muslims whom they used to mock, harm and humiliate in the world, saying: ﴿"Are these the ones about whom you swore that Allah would not grant them any mercy?"﴾, i.e., you swore. Then it is said to the companions of the Heights: ﴿"Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve"﴾.

In the third verse, Allah the Exalted says, informing about the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water, or from what Allah has provided you"﴾. This is because of the intensity of their thirst; ﴿"or from what Allah has provided you"﴾, i.e., from the food, because of the intensity of their hunger. So it is said to them: ﴿"Indeed, Allah has forbidden both of them"﴾, i.e., the drink and food of Paradise, ﴿"to the disbelievers"﴾, so they will never attain them in any circumstance.

Then He described the disbelievers to display their crimes which necessitated their deprivation and punishment, so that this would be an admonition and a lesson for the disbelievers of Quraysh and for all other people. This is what the fourth verse contains: ﴿Those who took their religion as diversion and amusement, and whom the worldly life deceived. So today We will forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs, and just as they used to deny Our signs﴾. That is, We will leave them in their punishment just as they left this day of theirs, not doing for it any of the faith and righteous deeds, and because of their denial of Our signs which call to faith and righteous deeds.

**Lessons from the verses:**

1. Wealth and men avail nothing at all for one who dies a disbeliever, a polytheist, of the people of wrongdoing and corruption.

2. Good tidings to the weak among the Muslims of entering Paradise and their happiness therein.

3. The prohibition of taking any part of the religion as diversion and amusement.

4. A warning against being deceived by the world to the point that a servant forgets his Hereafter, so that he has nothing left in it that benefits him, namely faith and righteous deeds.

The commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 52–54:

Explanation of the words:

*And We had certainly brought them a Book*: That is, the people of Makkah first, then all other people.

*A Book*: The Great Qur'an.

*We have detailed it with knowledge*: We have explained it with knowledge from Us, so We made clear its lawful and unlawful, its promises and threats, its narratives, its admonitions and its parables.

*Its interpretation (ta'wil)*: The ta'wil (final outcome, consequence) of what came in the Book of promise and threat, that is, the outcome of what they were warned of.

*And has strayed from them*: That is, it went away and they could not find it.

*In six days*: These are from Sunday to Friday.

*He covers the night over the day*: Each of them covers the other when it comes.

*Rapidly*: Quickly, without interruption.

*Subjected*: Made subservient.

*Unquestionably (alā)*: A particle of opening and alerting (like "hello" for the telephone).

*His is the creation and the command*: That is, His are the creatures and the disposal of them, He alone, without partner.

*Blessed (tabāraka)*: That is, His power is magnified, and His goodness and blessings are beyond limit.

*The worlds (al-ʿālamīn)*: Everything other than Allah the Exalted is an ʿālam, that is, a sign pointing to its Creator and its true God.

Meaning of the verses:

After that presentation of the states of people on the Day of Resurrection and the scenes of bliss and hellfire, Allah the Exalted informed that He has brought the Quraysh, for the sake of their guidance, a great Book, the noble Qur'an, and He detailed it in detail. He clarified tawhid and its proofs, shirk and its causes, obedience and its good effects, and disobedience and its evil effects in the present and in the final outcome. He made the Book a guidance, that is, a guide and a mercy by which the believers are guided and by which they are shown mercy.

This is what the first verse [52] contains, which is His saying: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾. As for the second verse [53], the Truth, the Exalted, there expressed slowness regarding the faith of the people of Makkah to whom He brought the detailed and clarified Book, so He said: ﴿Do they await except its ta'wil?﴾, that is, they do not await except the outcome of what the Qur'an informed of regarding the Resurrection and its terrors, and the Fire and its punishment. At that time they will believe. But would faith benefit them on that day? And here they are saying ﴿On the Day its ta'wil comes, those who had forgotten it before will say﴾, and the veil will be lifted from what was promised, ﴿"the messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth"﴾, that is, before its occurrence, and that was in the worldly life; they forgot it and did not act by what would save them from punishment. They acknowledged what they had been denying and rejecting. Then they wish for what will never be realized for them, saying: ﴿"Are there for us any intercessors who will intercede for us, or could we be returned"﴾ to the world ﴿"so we would do other than what we used to do"﴾ of shirk, evil and corruption. Their wishes go with the wind, and nothing reached them but the following proclamation: ﴿"They have certainly lost themselves, and lost from them is what they used to invent"﴾. They lost themselves in Hell, and every hope was lost to them, and what they used to invent was gone from them, namely that their gods and allies would intercede for them, save them from the Fire and admit them to Paradise.

In the last verse Allah the Exalted says to those who delay in their faith: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, who loves that you worship Him, call upon Him, draw near to Him and obey Him, ﴿is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne; He covers the night with the day, which it pursues rapidly, and [He created] the sun, the moon and the stars, subjected by His command﴾. This is your true Lord and your God, other than whom you have no god, and besides whom you have no lord. As for idols and images, they will never be a lord or a god to anyone, because they are created and not creators, incapable of benefiting themselves or repelling harm from themselves, so how [could they be] for others? Indeed your Lord and your true worshipped One, to whom belongs all creation in ownership and disposal, and to whom alone belongs the command, He disposes as He wills over all the dominion, its upper and its lower parts. So blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Guidance of the verses:

1. Faith does not benefit at the sight of death and punishment, just as it does not benefit on the Day of Resurrection.

2. Deliberation in affairs and patience in action, and avoiding haste, are good. Allah is capable of creating the heavens and the earth in an instant, but He created them in six days, the measure of worldly days, as teaching and guidance toward deliberation and patience in affairs.

3. One of the attributes of the Lord, the Exalted, which must be believed in and whose interpretation (ta'wil) or modality (takyif) is forbidden, is His establishment above His Throne.

4. The confinement of all creation to Him, the Exalted: there is no creator but Him, and likewise the command: there is no commander or prohibiter other than Him. Here ʿUmar said: "Whoever has anything left, let him seek it, since nothing remains, as long as creation and command both belong to Allah."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 55–56:

Explanation of the words:

"Ud'u rabbakum" (Call upon your Lord): ask Him for your needs, both of this world and of the Hereafter, for He is your Lord, so do not be shy of asking Him.

"Tadarru'an wa khufyah" (Humbly and secretly): that is, while you are humble and submissive, concealing the supplication and not raising your voices with it.

"Al-mu'tadin" (the transgressors): that is, in supplication and otherwise. Transgression in supplication is to ask Allah for what His custom does not grant, create or change, such as asking to become a prophet, or asking to bring back a child or a young boy, or raising one's voice in supplication.

"Wa la tufsidu fil-ardi" (And do not cause corruption on the earth): that is, by associating partners with Allah and by sins, after it has been set right by monotheism and acts of obedience.

"Al-muhsinin" (the good-doers): those who make their deeds and intentions good, by being mindful of Allah the Exalted in all their states.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted made His servants acquainted with Himself, that He is their true Lord and their God, and that He is the Creator, the Commander, in whose hand is the disposal of everything, He commanded them, as guidance for them, to call upon Him, and explained to them the state in which they should call upon Him, so that He would respond to them. He said: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾, that is, in humility and submission, and "secretly" means privately, not aloud. He forbade them from transgression in supplication, informing them that He does not love the transgressors. Transgression in supplication is to call upon other than Allah the Exalted, or to call upon another along with Him, and among it is seeking things that have causes without preparing their causes, or asking for what Allah's custom does not permit, such as a person asking to become a prophet, or to return from middle age to youth, or from youth to childhood.

Then, after this guidance and direction toward what perfects and makes them happy, He forbade them from corruption on the earth after He had set it right, and corruption on the earth occurs through associating partners with Allah and through sins. Sins include all forbidden acts, such as killing people, seizing their property, spoiling their crops, corrupting their minds through sorcery and narcotics, and violating their honour through adultery and other grave sins. Once more He urges them to call upon Him, because supplication is worship, and in the authentic hadith: "Supplication is worship" (al-du'a' huwa al-'ibadah). So He said: "Call upon your Lord," that is, ask Him for your needs while you are in your supplication fearful of His punishment and hopeful, longing for His mercy. He made clear to them that His mercy is near to the good-doers, those who make their intentions and deeds good, and among that is supplication: whoever makes his supplication good attains a response. So the reward of the good-doers is near at hand, unlike the evildoers, for they are not answered.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation to call upon Allah the Exalted, for supplication is worship.

2- The etiquette of supplication: that the one supplicating be humble and submissive, that he conceal his supplication and not voice it aloud, that he be in a state of fear and hope while supplicating, and that he not transgress in supplication by calling upon other than Allah the Exalted or by asking for what Allah's custom does not grant.

3- The prohibition of corruption on the earth through associating partners with Allah and through sins, after Allah the Exalted has set it right through Islam.

4- Encouragement toward good-doing in every sense, both particular and general, since Allah the Exalted loves its people.

He said: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾, that is, in humility and submission, and "secretly" means privately, not aloud. He forbade them from transgression in supplication, informing them that He does not love the transgressors. Transgression in supplication is to call upon other than Allah the Exalted, or to call upon another along with Him, and among it is seeking things that have causes without preparing their causes, or asking for what Allah's custom does not permit, such as a person asking to become a prophet, or to return from middle age to youth, or from youth to childhood.

Then, after this guidance and direction toward what perfects and makes them happy, He forbade them from corruption on the earth after He had set it right, and corruption on the earth occurs through associating partners with Allah and through sins. Sins include all forbidden acts, such as killing people, seizing their property, spoiling their crops, corrupting their minds through sorcery and narcotics, and violating their honour through adultery and other grave sins. Once more He urges them to call upon Him, because supplication is worship, and in the authentic hadith: "Supplication is worship" (al-du'a' huwa al-'ibadah). So He said: "Call upon your Lord," that is, ask Him for your needs while you are in your supplication fearful of His punishment and hopeful, longing for His mercy. He made clear to them that His mercy is near to the good-doers, those who make their intentions and deeds good, and among that is supplication: whoever makes his supplication good attains a response. So the reward of the good-doers is near at hand, unlike the evildoers, for they are not answered.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation to call upon Allah the Exalted, for supplication is worship.

2- The etiquette of supplication: that the one supplicating be humble and submissive, that he conceal his supplication and not voice it aloud, that he be in a state of fear and hope while supplicating, and that he not transgress in supplication by calling upon other than Allah the Exalted or by asking for what Allah's custom does not grant.

3- The prohibition of corruption on the earth through associating partners with Allah and through sins, after Allah the Exalted has set it right through Islam.

4- Encouragement toward good-doing in every sense, both particular and general, since Allah the Exalted loves its people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 57–58:

Explanation of the words:

Al-riyah (the winds): plural of rih, which is moving air.

Bushran: plural of bashir, meaning heralds of the nearness of rain. It is also read as nushran, meaning that they spread out the clouds for the rains.

Rahmatih (His mercy): that is, the mercy of God Most High, which is the rain.

Aqallat sahaban thiqalan: that is, they carried heavy clouds saturated with water vapour.

Mayyit (dead): having no plants, no herbage and no pasture.

Kadhalika nukhriju al-mawta: that is, in the same way We revive the dead and bring them forth from their graves alive.

Tadhakkarun: you may remember, and so believe in the Resurrection and the Recompense.

Al-tayyib (the good): that is, the good soil.

Khabutha: that is, its soil has become corrupt, being salt-marsh.

Illa nakidan: that is, only with difficulty.

Nusarrifu al-ayat: that is, We diversify them, vary their styles, and mention in some what is not mentioned in others, for guidance and instruction.

Li-qawmin yashkurun: because they are the ones who benefit from the blessings by thanking for them, by spending them in what pleases God Most High.

The meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues to explain the manifestations of divine power and the divine mercy that make it obligatory to worship Him alone, to the exclusion of all others. God Most High says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as heralds﴾. He, that is your Lord, the true one, there is no god but Him. "Bushran" means heralds, and "nushran" means that the winds spread out the clouds, carrying the heavy clouds so that He may water the dead earth, which then comes to life with crops and plants, so that you may eat and pasture your livestock. By a similar arrangement in sending down rain and reviving the earth after its death, He will revive you after your death, bringing you forth from your graves alive, to call you to account for your deeds in this abode, and to recompense you for them: good for good, and evil with its like, a just recompense in which there is no injustice. This act, which demonstrates power, mercy and subtle arrangement, He shows you, so that you see it with your own eyes, so that perhaps you may remember by it: that the One who is able to revive the dead land is able to revive dead bodies. Then you will believe in the meeting with your Lord and be certain of it, and act in accordance with what will make you happy and not wretched therein.

This is what the first verse [57] contains: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as heralds before His mercy﴾, that is, the rain, ﴿until, when they have carried heavy clouds﴾, that is, they have carried them, ﴿with water vapour﴾, ﴿We have driven them﴾, by Our power and the subtlety of Our arrangement, ﴿to a dead land﴾, having no life in it, no plants, no crops, and no herbage, ﴿and sent down by it﴾, that is, by means of the cloud, ﴿water﴾, sweet and pure, ﴿and We brought forth by it of all kinds of fruits﴾, varying in colours, scents and tastes, ﴿Thus We bring forth the dead﴾, just as this bringing forth of plants from the dead earth, We bring forth the dead from their graves. We have done this, We let you hear it and show it to you with your own eyes, in hope that you may remember, and so remember that the One who can revive the earth can revive the dead, as a mercy from Us to you and a kindness from Us towards you.

As for the second verse [58], it contains a parable which God Most High struck for the believing servant and the disbelieving one, following the explanation of His power to revive people after their death. God Most High says: ﴿And the good land﴾, that is, good in soil, ﴿its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾, this being after the rain is sent down upon it. This is a parable of the believing servant who has a living and good heart: when he hears what is sent down of the verses, his faith increases and his righteous deeds multiply. ﴿And that which is corrupt﴾, that is, the land whose soil is foul, salt-marsh or muddy, when rain falls on it, its vegetation comes forth only with difficulty, meagre and unfit. This is a parable of the disbeliever who, when he hears the Qur'anic verses, does not incline towards them and does not benefit from them in his character or conduct, so he does neither good nor refrains from evil.

And His saying: ﴿Thus We diversify the signs﴾, that is, by explaining the manifestations of His power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, and by striking parables and presenting proofs and lessons, ﴿for a people who give thanks﴾, since they are the ones who benefit from them. As for the disbelieving deniers, how can they benefit from them, when they do not recognise good nor deny evil?

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The affirmation of the creed of the Resurrection and of life after death for reckoning and recompense, for it is one of the most important pillars of faith.

2- Inference from the present to the unseen, which is among the beneficial sciences.

3- The excellence of striking parables to bring meanings closer to minds.

4- The virtue of gratitude, which is spending a blessing on the purpose for which God Most High bestowed it upon the servant.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Nuhan* (Noah): This is the first of the messengers. This grateful servant is Nuh ibn Lamak ibn Mutawshalakh ibn Akhnukh, i.e., Idris, peace be upon them both. He is one of the five *ulu al-azm* (possessors of resolve) among the messengers. He lived as a caller, guide and teacher for 1,240 years, and the duration of his calling was a thousand years minus fifty years. What came after that he lived as a guide and teacher to the believers.

*Adhaba yawmin 'azim* (the punishment of a great day): This is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

*Al-mala'* (the chiefs): The nobles and leaders of the people, who fill the eye and the assembly.

*Wa-ansahu lakum* (and I advise you): I want good for you and nothing else.

*Awa 'ajibtum* (Do you wonder?): The interrogative is for denial. *'Ajibtum* is joined by the conjunctive *waw* to the preceding clause, which is *kadhdhabtum* (you denied), i.e., "Did you deny and wonder?"

*Liyundhirakum* (to warn you): i.e., of the punishment that follows from disbelief and sins.

*Wa-litattaqu* (and that you may fear [Allah]): i.e., Allah the Exalted, by faith in Him, affirming His oneness and obeying Him, so that you may be shown mercy and not be punished.

*Wal-ladhina ma'ahu fi al-fulk* (and those with him in the ark): These are the believers among his people. *Al-fulk* is the ship that he built by the command and help of Allah the Exalted.

*'Amin* (blind): Plural of *'amm*, one blind in insight. As for one blind in the eyes, the term used is *a'mى* (blind).

**Meaning of the Verses:**

This begins the mention of the stories of six of the messengers: Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, Shu'ayb and Musa, peace be upon them. The purpose of mentioning these stories is to vary the method of calling, so that those being called, the disbelievers of Quraysh, may see living images and vivid scenes of past peoples: how their beginnings were and how their ends concluded. These do not differ much from the events of the call they are living and the conflict raging between them and their prophet, so that perhaps they will take warning. Moreover, the stories establish the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, for had he not been a messenger to whom revelation is sent, he could not have related reports of the past that dazzle the minds. Likewise, the believers with their prophet gain lessons that move them to steadfastness and patience, and keep them from despair and hopelessness regarding a good outcome, victory and triumph.

This is the first story in which Allah says: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people﴾, i.e., by Our might, We sent Noah to his people just as We sent you, O Our Messenger, to your people, both Arabs and non-Arabs. So he said, i.e., Noah in his call: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him﴾, i.e., there is truly no god for you besides Him, for the true God is the one who creates, provides, governs, gives life and causes death, bestows and withholds, harms and benefits, hears and sees. How does this compare with the gods you have carved with your hands and placed in your houses, blind and unable to see, deaf and unable to hear, mute and unable to speak? How could it be proper to call them god and worship them? ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾: he warned them of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection if they persist in polytheism and disobedience. Then the chiefs among them answered him, and they were the people of authority and decision in the land, saying: ﴿Indeed, we see you in manifest error﴾, because of this hostile stance of yours toward our gods and our worship of them. He, peace be upon him, replied, saying: ﴿O my people, there is no error in me﴾, meaning not even a mere error, let alone total error as you claim. ﴿But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., to you. ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord and I advise you﴾, i.e., with what is good for you in your present state and your final end. And know that ﴿I know from Allah what you do not know﴾: I have knowledge of the greatness, authority, majesty and beauty of my Lord, of His mercy and kindness, and of His retribution and punishment, while you do not know. So fear Allah and obey me, and He will forgive you your sins and delay you until your appointed terms, and not hasten your annihilation. He continued his speech with them, and it lasted a thousand years minus fifty, saying: Did you deny what I called you to and brought you? And do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you and that you may fear Allah by affirming His oneness, worshipping Him and obeying Him, in hope that you may be shown mercy and not be punished? Does wise people wonder at this?

The result of this blessed and good call was that they denied him, so his Lord saved him and the believers with him, and drowned those who denied Our signs, because they were a blind people, and so did not deserve survival and salvation. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people﴾: unable to perceive the signs, and unable to see the warnings and evidences.

**Lessons from the Verses:**

1. Affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, like the prophethood of Noah, peace be upon him.
2. Affirmation and confirmation of monotheism, and explanation of the meaning of "there is no god but Allah."
3. Warning against the punishment of the Day of Resurrection by reminding of it.
4. Those who hold benefits of position and the like are the ones who reject the call to truth, because it contradicts falsehood.
5. Establishment of the principle that the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing.
6. Blindness of the heart is more dangerous to its owner than blindness of the eyes.
