Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 65–69:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa-ila 'Ad* (And to 'Ad): That is, "And We certainly sent to the tribe of 'Ad." 'Ad was the ancestor of the tribe, namely 'Ad ibn 'Awess ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh (peace be upon him).

*Akhahum Hudan* (their brother Hud): a brother to them in lineage, not in religion. Hud is Hud ibn Shalikh ibn Arfakhshad ibn Sam ibn Nuh (peace be upon him).

*Afala tattaqun* (Will you not then fear [Allah]?): That is, "Will you persist in polytheism and not guard yourselves against the punishment of Allah by believing in Him and affirming His oneness?" The interrogative is one of rebuke, meaning he censures them for not being mindful of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

*Fi safaha* (in folly): safaha is like safah, meaning lightness of intellect, lack of perception and forbearance.

*Amin* (trustworthy): I will not betray you, nor deceive you, nor lie to you; just as I am trusted with my message and do not fall short in conveying it.

*Bastah* (stature): That is, height and bulk of bodies, for they were giants because of the greatness and tallness of their bodies.

*Ala' Allah* (the bounties of Allah): His blessings; its singular forms are ala, ali, aly and alw, and the plural is ala'.

*Tuflihun* (you may prosper): by being saved from the Fire in the Hereafter and from ruin in this world.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the second narrative, the story of Hud (peace be upon him) with his people 'Ad the First, whom Allah the Exalted destroyed with a furious, roaring wind that He subjected against them for seven nights and eight days. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And to 'Ad﴾: that is, "And We sent to the tribe of 'Ad their brother in lineage, Hud." So what did he say to them? ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah﴾: that is, make Him one in worship and do not worship alongside Him other gods. And His saying: ﴿You have no god other than Him﴾: that is, there is no god for you besides Allah, for Allah is the true God and whatever else is worshipped is a false god, because He creates while they create nothing, He provides sustenance while they provide none, and He governs life in all that it contains, while they are themselves governed; they possess neither benefit nor harm, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection. How, then, could they be gods? Then he urged them toward piety and rebuked them for abandoning it, so he (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿Will you not then fear [Allah]?﴾: that is, Allah, your Lord, so that you abandon polytheism and make Him one? But the chiefs of his people who disbelieved answered him with the worst of replies, out of their arrogance and deception, saying: ﴿Indeed, we see you in folly﴾: that is, in foolishness, levity, and lack of insight into life; for how else would you depart from the consensus of your people and confront them with the faults of their gods and the folly of their judgment? ﴿And indeed, we think you are among the liars﴾ regarding what you have brought, namely the message and the call to monotheism and the rejection of gods other than Allah, the Exalted.

Hud (peace be upon him) answered, refuting their accusation, and said: ﴿O my people, there is no folly in me, but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾: that is, I am not as you claim, that there is folly in me; rather I bear a message that I convey to you, and in this I am a sincere advisor to you, desiring good for you, trustworthy concerning the revelation of Allah the Exalted to me, trustworthy: I do not deceive you nor betray you, for I desire nothing for you but good. Then he continued his call, saying: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you﴾: that is, do you deny my messages and wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come, ﴿through a man from among you, so that he may warn you﴾ of the consequences of your disbelief and polytheism? Is it from such a thing that sensible people wonder, or are you without understanding?

Then he reminded them of Allah's blessings upon them, perhaps they would bring to their minds some remembrance, so that they might turn back after their obstinacy and persistence. He said: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Nuh﴾: that is, after He destroyed them with the flood for their persistence in polytheism. ﴿And He increased you broadly in creation﴾: that is, He made your bodies strong and your statures tall; these are the blessings of Allah upon you. ﴿So remember the bounties of Allah that you may prosper﴾: for if you remember them in your hearts, you will thank Him with your words and deeds, and by that your prosperity is completed for you, which is your deliverance from what is feared and your triumph in what is loved, and that is the desired success.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The call to worship Allah and to abandon the worship of anything other than Him, which is the meaning of "There is no god but Allah."

2- The legitimacy of repelling an accusation and clearing oneself of the falsehood with which one is charged.

3- Among the duties of the Messengers (peace be upon them) is conveying what they were commanded to convey.

4- The virtue of sincere advice and the character of trustworthiness.

5- The commendability of reminding people of blessings, for this brings about gratitude and obedience.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 70–72:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-nadhar (ونذر): i.e., we abandon.

Bi-ma ta'iduna (بما تعدنا): i.e., of the punishment.

Rijs (رجسٌ): wrath that necessitates punishment.

Atujadilunani (أتجادلونني): i.e., do you dispute with me.

Min sultan (من سلطان): i.e., any proof or clear evidence establishing that they deserve worship.

Dabir (دابر): the dabir of a people is their last member, because when the last of a people perishes, their first also perishes, without doubt.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Hud, peace be upon him. Here they are, responding to Hud's call through the words of the chiefs among them: ﴿Have you come to us that we should worship Allah alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship?﴾ and they threatened him that if we do not give up worshipping our gods, ﴿then bring us what you threaten us with﴾ of punishment, ﴿if you are of the truthful﴾ in your claim. So Hud, peace be upon him, replied to this statement of theirs, saying: wrath and anger from Allah, the Exalted, has already befallen you, and your punishment has therefore become expected every day, so wait for what will befall you. ﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We saved him and those with him by mercy from Us﴾ — i.e., after the descent of the punishment, and those who were with him of the believers by a mercy from Us specifically, which is not granted except to their like. ﴿And We cut off the last of those who denied Our signs and were not believers﴾ — We destroyed them with a violent wind that destroys everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing could be seen but their dwellings. And thus is the recompense of the wrongdoers.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The polytheists' argument for the validity of their falsehood by the deeds of their fathers and forefathers is almost a consistent custom among nations and peoples, and it is blameworthy imitation (taqlid).

2- Among the folly of the disbelievers is their hastening of the punishment and their demanding it.

3- The gods of idol-worshippers are mere names with no realities, since a person's applying the name of god to a stone does not make it a god that benefits, harms, gives life and causes death.

4- The power of Allah, the Exalted, and His kindness are manifested in the destruction of 'Ad and the salvation of Hud and the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 73–76:

Explanation of the words:

And to Thamud: that is, We sent [a messenger] to Thamud. Thamud was a tribe named after its forefather, Thamud ibn Aabir ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh.

Their brother Salih: that is, in lineage. Salih is Salih ibn Ubayd ibn Asif ibn Kashih ibn Ubayd ibn Hadhir ibn Thamud.

A sign (ayah): a proof of the truth of my claim that I am the messenger of Allah to you.

And He settled you in the land: He placed you in dwellings in which you take pleasure.

And you hew: you carve out the rocks in the mountains so that you may take them as dwellings to inhabit.

The favours of Allah (ala' Allah): the blessings of Allah, the Exalted, which are many.

And do not spread corruption (la ta'thaw): that is, do not corrupt in the land, being corrupters.

Waxed arrogant (istakbaru): they transgressed, rebelled and became proud, so they did not accept the truth nor acknowledge it.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the third narrative, the story of the Prophet of Allah, Salih, peace be upon him. The Exalted said: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih﴾, meaning: And We sent to the tribe of Thamud their brother Salih as a prophet, whom We sent with the same message that Our messengers before and after him were sent with, the word of monotheism, ﴿He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him."﴾ This is the meaning of the word of sincerity brought by the Seal of the Prophets: "There is no deity but Allah." ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord﴾ testifying that there is no deity but Him and that I am His messenger to you. This clear evidence was a she-camel that came out of a rock in a mountain. ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you﴾, a sign, and what a sign, of the truth of my being sent by Allah, the Exalted, as a messenger to you, so that you worship Him alone and do not associate anything with Him. ﴿So leave her to eat in the earth of Allah, and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you.﴾ The she-camel used to graze in the pasture and come to the people's water and drink it all, and it would turn in her belly into pure milk, so they milked as much as they wished. He said to them one day: "This is a she-camel with a turn to drink, and you have a turn to drink on a known day. Do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a great day seize you." He, peace be upon him, admonished them with his saying: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad﴾, meaning after their destruction. The dwellings of 'Ad were in Hadramawt in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, and the dwellings of Thamud were in al-Hijr in the north of the Peninsula, between the Hijaz and al-Sham. His saying ﴿and settled you in the land﴾: in the land of al-Hijr, you take from its plains palaces in which you dwell in the summer, and you hew from the mountains houses in which you dwell in the winter. ﴿So remember the favours of Allah﴾, that is, His great blessings, so that you may thank Him by worshipping Him alone, rather than the idols you have taken. He warned them against the consequences of corruption, saying: ﴿And do not spread corruption in the land, being corrupters﴾, that is, do not spread corruption in the land through association and committing sins. In the face of this sincere call, aimed at guiding the people and reforming them so that they may be saved from the consequences of shirk, evil and corruption: ﴿The eminent ones of his people who had waxed arrogant said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed﴾, that is, to the believers from among the weak of the people: ﴿Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?﴾ This was a question of mockery and derision, indicating the arrogance and pride of the people. The believers among the weak people answered, saying: ﴿Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent﴾. They said it clearly, plainly, and openly declaring their faith in what the Messenger of Allah, Salih, had brought, not fearing. Here the arrogant replied, saying: ﴿Indeed, we are disbelievers in that in which you have believed﴾. In their obstinacy and arrogance, they went to excess and did not say "we disbelieve in what he was sent with," so as not to acknowledge the messengerhood even in the answer to the reply, so they said ﴿Indeed, we are disbelievers in that in which you have believed﴾.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The unity of the message of the messengers in faith in Allah and rejection of tyranny (taghut), that is, in the worship of Allah alone.

2- Affirmation that the messengers were sent with signs, which are miracles, and the sign of Salih was the most wondrous sign, namely the she-camel.

3- The obligation to remind of Allah's blessings, since that is what prompts gratitude, and gratitude is obedience.

4- The prohibition of corruption in the land, of shirk, and of committing sins.

5- The weak are generally the followers of the prophets, because they are free of the impediments such as the preservation of position, rank or wealth, and their not being immersed in pleasures and desires.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 77–79:

Explanation of the words:

"Fa-'aqarū al-nāqata" (so they hamstrung the she-camel): they cut its legs and then slaughtered it. Hamstringing (ʿaqr) means cutting the legs. The she-camel was the sign (āyah).

"Wa-ʿataw ʿan amri rabbihim" (and they transgressed against the command of their Lord): they rebelled against the command and disobeyed, not obeying it.

"Al-rajfah" (the violent quake): the single instance of the verb rajafa, meaning to be agitated. When they heard the Cry, the quake seized them.

"Jāthimīn" (lying prostrate): kneeling on their knees as a bird crouches, that is, dead upon their knees.

"Fa-tawalla ʿanhum" (then he turned away from them): after they had perished, Ṣāliḥ looked at them as they lay prostrate, and, lamenting their condition, said, "﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord﴾" up to His words "﴿but you do not like sincere advisors﴾." Then he turned away from them and departed.

The meaning of the verses:

The narrative about Ṣāliḥ (peace be upon him) continues. After that long and broad call, the arrogant ones rejected it with insolence and pride. They demanded a sign to demonstrate his truthfulness and that he was among the messengers. They were given the she-camel as a clear sign, but they persisted in dispute and obstinacy. Finally, they conspired to kill the she-camel and hamstrung her. ﴿So their Lord crushed them over their sin, and leveled them, and He does not fear its consequence﴾ [al-Shams: 14–15].

Regarding His saying in the first verse [77]: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and transgressed against the command of their Lord﴾. Exalted is He, Who informs that the people of Ṣāliḥ hamstrung the she-camel, cutting her legs, and then slaughtered her; this is ʿaqr. By this they transgressed and became proud, rebelling against the command of God, Exalted is He, Who had instructed them to leave her to graze on God's earth and not to harm her with evil. Yet they hamstrung her out of defiance and obstinacy. ﴿And they said, "O Ṣāliḥ"﴾ instead of saying "O Messenger of God" or "O Prophet of God", ﴿"bring us what you threaten us with"﴾, that is, the punishment, if we touched the she-camel with harm. Now we have slaughtered her, so bring us the punishment if you are, as you claim, among the messengers. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So the quake seized them﴾, which was a violent shaking by which hearts and souls trembled, as a result of a Cry from a mighty angel who called out to them on Saturday morning, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So the Cry seized them at sunrise﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 73]. When they perished, Ṣāliḥ stood over them as one bidding farewell, just as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood over the people of the well at Badr, calling to them, "O so-and-so, O so-and-so." Likewise Ṣāliḥ, upon him and our Prophet be blessings and peace, stood over them while they were lifeless and said, lamenting and grieving: ﴿"O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord, and advised you, but you do not like sincere advisors"﴾, and he turned away from them and departed.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The descent of God's vengeance upon whoever rebels against His command, glory be to Him.

2- The legitimacy of lamentation (rithāʾ) for one who has died or been struck by a great calamity.

3- A sign of the nearness of the hour of destruction is when people dislike advice and do not love those who give it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 80–84:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-Lūṭan (And Lot): That is, "And We sent Lot." Lot is Lot son of Haran, the nephew of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He was born in Babylon, Iraq.

Al-fāḥisha (the abomination): It is the ugly deed, namely, men coming to men in their backsides.

Min al-'ālamīn (from among the worlds): That is, from among mankind.

Min al-ghābirīn (among those who remained behind): Those left behind in the punishment.

Wa-amṭarnā (And We rained down): We sent down upon them stones from the sky like rain, and so We destroyed them.

Al-mujrimīn (the criminals): That is, those who corrupt beliefs, morals and honour.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the fourth of the stories, the story of Allah's Prophet Lot son of Haran, the nephew of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The words of Allah, ﴿And Lot...﴾, mean: And We sent Lot to his people, the people of Sodom. Lot was not one of them, for he came from the land of Babylon, Iraq, emigrating with his uncle Ibrahim, and Allah sent him to the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, near the Dead Sea (Buhayrat Lūṭ) in Jordan.

And His words, when he said to his people to whom he was sent, denouncing their reprehensible deed: ﴿Do you commit an abomination such as no one in the worlds has preceded you in?﴾ That is, no one among mankind at all had preceded you in it. He continued denouncing this vice, rebuking these people whose morals had sunk to a depth to which no one else had sunk, saying: ﴿Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed limits.﴾ Otherwise, the desire for women is what humans are naturally disposed to, not the backsides of men; rather, it is criminality, plunging into evil and corruption, and extravagance in that. Extravagance has no end point for its perpetrator.

After this admonition and guidance to the path of salvation, and to escaping this predicament into which these extravagant people had fallen, their response was none other than ﴿that they said: "Expel them"﴾, that is, Lot and the believers with him, ﴿from your town﴾, that is, your city of Sodom, justifying the expulsion of them from the land on the grounds that they are people who keep themselves pure from the filth in which they are immersed. When the matter had reached this point, Allah said: ﴿So We saved him and his family﴾, from his daughters and some of his wives, ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remained behind﴾. For he had commanded them to leave the land by night before the punishment descended upon the people, and they left. As soon as they had departed the region, Allah turned its upper part to its lower part and rained down upon it stones of baked clay (sijjīl), and they were all destroyed.

And His words at the conclusion of this story: ﴿So observe how was the end of the criminals﴾ — this is a general address to everyone who hears this story, so that he may take a lesson from it, having witnessed the end of the criminals: complete destruction and painful punishment.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The extreme ugliness of the crime of sodomy (liwāṭ).

2- The first people known to have committed this filthy crime were the people of Lot (peace be upon him).

3- Extravagance and lack of moderation in words and deeds give rise to every evil and corruption.

4- Disbelief and criminality dissolve the bond of brotherhood and kinship between their adherents and those who are innocent of them.

Whoever commits this abomination from among the married (muḥṣanīn) is stoned to death.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 85–87:

Explanation of the words:

{And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb}: Madyan is the father of the tribe, namely Madyan ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil, and Shu'ayb was from the descendants of the tribe. Thus he was their brother by lineage in truth, for he was Shu'ayb ibn Mika'il ibn Yashjur ibn Madyan.

{And do not diminish for the people their things}: That is, do not reduce the people's valuation of their goods and merchandise, for they used to do this.

{On every path, threatening}: A path; "threatening" means frightening the passers-by and taking tolls from them, or stripping them of their belongings.

{And seeking to make it crooked}: That is, you desire the way of Allah, which is His law, to be crooked so that it agrees with your inclinations.

{The corrupters}: They are those who commit sins in the land.

{Will judge between us}: He will decide between us, saving the believers and destroying the disbelievers.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the fifth narrative in Surat al-A'raf, the narrative of the Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb with his people, the people of Madyan. His saying, exalted is He, {And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb}, means: and We sent to the people of Madyan their brother Shu'ayb. What did he say to them when he was sent to them? {He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him."} That is, say: there is no god but Allah. It necessarily follows that they believe in the Messenger Shu'ayb, so that they may worship Allah in the manner He loves to be worshipped and in what befits perfecting them and making them happy in both abodes. And his saying, {There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord}, means: a manifest sign testifying to my messengerhood, and that what I command you and forbid you from is from Allah, exalted is He. Therefore, {Give full measure and weight in justice}, that is, with equity, which is justice. {And do not diminish for the people their things} but give them what their goods deserve in price according to their quality and inferiority. {And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation}: that is, in the lands after their reformation, and that is by abandoning polytheism and sins, and among that is abandoning robbery and highway banditry, and abandoning fraud in measure and weight, and not diminishing the people's goods and merchandise. {That is better for you, if you are believers}: that which I call you to, of obedience and abandoning disobedience, is better for you in condition and outcome.

And his saying: {And do not sit on every path, threatening and barring from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked}: he, peace be upon him, forbids them from the most heinous crime, which is that they sit at the entrances of the land and at the mouths of the roads, threatening the passers-by with punishment if they associate with the Prophet Shu'ayb and sit with him, turning people away from faith and uprightness. Likewise, they cut the roads, strip people of their garments and belongings, or impose a special tax upon them.

His saying: {And remember when you were few and He increased you} reminds them, peace be upon him, of the blessing of Allah upon them, which is that they became a great people after they had been a small people, of no worth or weight among the peoples. His saying: {And observe how was the end of the corrupters} admonishes them by showing the fate of the oppressive corrupters among the neighboring nations and peoples, where the vengeance of Allah descended upon them and His punishment fell upon them, so they perished. He admonishes them so that perhaps they will remember, abandon polytheism and sins, and act upon monotheism and obedience.

Finally, he warns them by Allah, exalted is He, and threatens them that a just judge, who is Allah, will judge between them, and then they will know who is the righteous and who is the wrongdoer. So he said: {And if there is a group among you who have believed in that with which I have been sent}, that is, a community, {and a group who has not believed}, and by this we are disputing and in need of one who will judge between us. Therefore, {be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges}.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The call of the messengers is one in matters of belief, for all of it rests upon the foundation of monotheism and obedience.

2- The prohibition of fraud in measure and weight, and of diminishing the people's goods; this includes crafts, trades, and the like.

3- The prohibition of corruption on the earth through sins, especially in lands that Allah has purified with Islam and reformed with its laws.

4- The prohibition of robbery, highway banditry, and frightening passers-by.

5- The prohibition of barring from the way of Allah by preventing people from religiosity and adherence to the law, outwardly and inwardly.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 88–89:

Explanation of the words:

Al-mala' (the notables): the chiefs of the people, who fill the assembly when they sit and draw the eye when they are looked at.

Istakbaru (they showed arrogance): they feigned greatness while they were in fact contemptible, so that they would not accept the truth.

Min qaryatina (from our town): from our city.

Fi millatikum (into your religion): into your faith.

ʿAla Allahi tawakkalna (in God we have put our trust): that is, we have entrusted our affair to Him and relied upon Him for our protection.

Rabbana iftah baynana (our Lord, judge between us): that is, O our Lord, decide between us.

Wa anta khayr al-fatihin (and You are the best of those who decide): that is, and You are the best of those who judge.

The meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues with the account of Shuʿayb and his people, the people of Madyan. After he had commanded them, forbidden them, reminded them and admonished them, ﴿The notables who showed arrogance among his people said﴾, threatening, promising and swearing: ﴿"O Shuʿayb, we will surely drive you out, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion."﴾ Such is the custom of the tyrannical oppressors: when they are overcome by proofs and evidence, they resort to force. When Shuʿayb, the orator of the prophets, peace be upon them, silenced them and cut off their path, they brandished the sword against him, namely exile and expulsion from the land, or a return to their false religion. ﴿"O Shuʿayb, we will surely drive you out, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion."﴾ Shuʿayb answered this threat by saying: ﴿"Even though we were averse?"﴾, that is: would we return to your religion even if we were averse to it? ﴿We would have forged a lie against God if we returned to your religion after God had rescued us from it.﴾ The lie against God, should they return to the religion of falsehood, lies in the fact that Shuʿayb had told them that God commanded them to worship Him alone and abandon the worship of others, and that He sent him to them as a messenger and commanded them to obey him, to rescue them from the falsehood in which they were. So if he, and those believing with him, were to apostatize and return to the religion of polytheism, their position would be that of one who lies against God, claiming that He said such-and-such when God, Mighty and Majestic, had not said it. Then Shuʿayb said: ﴿It is not for us to return to it﴾, it is neither possible nor feasible for us to return to your religion at all, except that our Lord should will something; for His will is executed upon His creation. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 88–89:

Explanation of the words:

Al-mala' (the notables): the chiefs of the people, who fill the assembly when they sit and draw the eye when they are looked at.

Istakbaru (they showed arrogance): they feigned greatness while they were in fact contemptible, so that they would not accept the truth.

Min qaryatina (from our town): from our city.

Fi millatikum (into your religion): into your faith.

ʿAla Allahi tawakkalna (in God we have put our trust): that is, we have entrusted our affair to Him and relied upon Him for our protection.

Rabbana iftah baynana (our Lord, judge between us): that is, O our Lord, decide between us.

Wa anta khayr al-fatihin (and You are the best of those who decide): that is, and You are the best of those who judge.

The meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues with the account of Shuʿayb and his people, the people of Madyan. After he had commanded them, forbidden them, reminded them and admonished them, ﴿The notables who showed arrogance among his people said﴾, threatening, promising and swearing: ﴿"O Shuʿayb, we will surely drive you out, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion."﴾ Such is the custom of the tyrannical oppressors: when they are overcome by proofs and evidence, they resort to force. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 90–93:

Explanation of the words:

"لئن اتبعتم شعيباً" (La'in ittaba'tum Shu'ayban): i.e., in following what he brought of religion and guidance.

"الرجفة" (al-Rajfah): violent shaking, like an earthquake.

"جاثمين" (jathimin): crouching on their knees, dead.

"كأن لم يغنوا فيها" (ka'an lam yaghnaw fiha): i.e., as if they had never inhabited it and dwelt there for a long time.

"الخاسرين" (al-khasirin): for they perished in this world and entered the Fire in the Hereafter.

"آسى" (asa): i.e., I grieve or feel extreme sorrow.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the story of Shu'ayb with the people of Madyan. After the wrongdoers threatened Shu'ayb with expulsion from their city, him and the believers with him, or that they would return to their creed, Shu'ayb answered the threat in a way that made them despair of returning to their religion. He sought refuge in God, declaring his reliance upon Him and asking for His just judgment between him and his idolatrous, wrongdoing people. It is as if the people were in turmoil, and some of them said: "Leave the man to what he is upon, and do not expose yourselves to trials you cannot bear." At this point, the eminent ones among his people who had been arrogant, swearing by false gods, said: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb﴾, i.e., in his religion, what he brought, and what he calls to of monotheism, justice, and the removal of oppression, ﴿then indeed you would be losers﴾. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So the shaking seized them﴾, in response to Shu'ayb's supplication, and they became dead, crouching on their knees. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, it was as if they had never dwelt there﴾, i.e., as if they had never inhabited the dwellings and resided in them for a long time. He emphasized this report, which is a judgment against the wrongdoing deniers, saying: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb—they were the losers﴾. As for those who affirmed Shu'ayb, they are the successful and the triumphant. Shu'ayb bid farewell to them, just as Salih bade farewell to his people. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So he turned away from them﴾, while they lay dead, and said: ﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, but you refused except to deny me, reject my words, and persist in polytheism and corruption until you were destroyed﴾. ﴿So how could I grieve over a disbelieving people?﴾, i.e., there is no sense in grief and sorrow over the likes of you.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The fruit of patience and steadfastness is victory, whether swift or deferred.

2. The end of injustice and tyranny is destruction and loss.

3. There is no grief or sorrow over those whom God the Exalted has destroyed for their wrongdoing and corruption on earth.

4. It is permissible to rebuke wrongdoers after their destruction, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did with the people of the well, and as Salih and Shu'ayb (peace be upon them) did.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 94–95:

Explanation of the words:

"In a town" (fi qaryah): the qaryah is the central city that gathers the notables of the land and its leaders; it is the city itself.

"With adversity" (bil-ba'sa'): with hardship, such as famine, hunger and wars.

"And affliction" (wal-darra'): a harmful condition, such as sicknesses, high prices and severe want of provision.

"Humble themselves" (yad'arun): they call upon Allah the Exalted and humble themselves before Him, so that He may remove the evil from them.

"In place of evil, good" (makan al-sayyi'ah al-hasanah): that is, in place of high prices, plenty; in place of fear, security; in place of sickness, health.

"Until they multiplied" (hatta 'afaw): their goods increased, their wealth grew, and all their conditions became good.

"Suddenly" (aakhadhnahum baghtah): We sent down punishment upon them unexpectedly.

Meaning of the two verses:

Following the account of the stories of five prophets, the Exalted mentioned His practice regarding the earlier nations, so that this would be an admonition to the Quraysh disbelievers and a reminder to the believers. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send a prophet into any town﴾, meaning, to the people of a town, and by the town is meant the metropolis and capital among the great cities, where the notables and leaders are, one of the prophets and messengers, and his people denied him and rejected his call, insisting on polytheism and error. Allah the Exalted then seizes the people of that city with kinds of disciplinary punishment, such as famine, hunger, hardship of life, sicknesses and wars, which is expressed by "adversity and affliction," in hope that they would return to the truth after their aversion to it, and accept it after turning away from it. Then the Exalted changes what they have of adversity and affliction into ease and plenty, and well-being and comfort, so that their wealth and children increase, and their rulers become strong. And when they are admonished and reminded, they say, so that they may repent, believe and fear God: ﴿Surely our fathers were touched by adversity and affliction﴾, meaning good and evil, and there is nothing here that you frighten us with; these are only the days, such as the turns of fortune: one day of hardship and another of ease. By this, the punishment becomes due upon them, and the Almighty, the Mighty and Majestic, seizes them suddenly ﴿while they perceive not﴾, so their destruction is completed, and they become a matter of lesson for those after them: punishment in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.

Guidance from the two verses:

1. Explanation of Allah's practice regarding the earlier nations.

2. A warning to the Quraysh disbelievers by what this practice indicates: that Allah seizes those who insist on disbelief and rebel against the truth.

3. Reminder and admonition through the history of earlier nations, which reveals the causes of their destruction and loss, so that the wise may avoid them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is certainly in their stories a lesson for people of understanding﴾ [Yusuf: 111].

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 96–100:

Explanation of the words:

*Amanu wa-ttaqu* (believed and feared God): that is, believe in God and His Messenger, and in the promise and threat of God, and fear Him, the Exalted, by obeying Him and not disobeying Him.

*Barakat min al-sama' wa-l-ard* (blessings from the heavens and the earth): the plural of *barakah* (blessing), which is the continuance and endurance of good. Knowledge and inspiration, and rain, are among the blessings of the heavens; plants, fertility, prosperity, security and well-being are among the blessings of the earth.

*Yaksibun* (they earn): through polytheism and sins.

*Bayatan* (by night): that is, at night while they are asleep.

*Makr Allah* (the plotting of God): His gradual leading of them on by showering blessings upon them, such as health of body and ease of living, until, when they feel secure from His plotting, He seizes them suddenly.

*Aw lam yahdi lahum* (or has it not become clear to them): that is, has it not been made clear to them, meaning, has it not become evident to them.

*Bi-dhunubihim* (for their sins): that is, because of their sins.

Meaning of the verses:

After the Exalted has explained His way with the earlier nations, which is that He seizes a people after their denial and disobedience with misfortune and hardship, and then, when they do not repent and persist in their unbelief and disobedience, He showers good things upon them until they become heedless through the abundance of their wealth and the improvement of their condition, and then seizes them suddenly and destroys them, so that their loss is complete in both abodes, He opens the door of repentance and hope to His servants, saying: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and feared God﴾, those who denied, such as the disbelievers of Makkah and Ta'if and other cities, ﴿had believed﴾, that is, in God and His Messenger, and in the meeting with God and His promise and threat, ﴿and feared God﴾ by abandoning polytheism and disobedience to Him and to His Messenger, ﴿We would surely have opened to them blessings from the heavens and the earth.﴾ He would have opened to them the gates of heaven with mercies and blessings, opened to them the treasures of the earth, and provided them with good things. But the earlier people of the towns denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn. As for the people of the towns today, who are also deniers, either they take warning from what befell the people of the earlier towns and believe, affirm the divine oneness and obey, or they persist in polytheism and denial, and there will descend upon them what descended upon those before them, the punishment of annihilation and uprooting. This is what the first verse [96] indicates, which is His saying: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and feared God, We would surely have opened to them blessings from the heavens and the earth. But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn.﴾ As for the three verses that follow, God rebukes the people of the towns for their heedlessness, reproaching them for their persistence and insistence upon falsehood, and marvelling at their condition, He says: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping?﴾ That is, are they ignorant of what befell those before them, so that they feel secure that Our punishment will come upon them at night while they are asleep? ﴿Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will come upon them in the morning while they are at play?﴾ That is, or have the people of the towns become heedless and felt secure that Our punishment will come upon them in the forenoon while they are busy with their works, which bring them no good, as if they were the play of children? ﴿Do they feel secure from the plotting of God?﴾ Has Our respite for them and Our gradual leading of them on deceived them into feeling secure from the plotting of God? **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 101–102:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Tilka al-qura* (those towns): a reference to the peoples of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb.

*Min anba'iha* (of their news): that is, of their accounts.

*Bil-bayyinat* (with clear proofs): with the arguments and demonstrations that point to the oneness of God and the truthfulness of His messengers.

*Min qabl* (before): that is, before their creation and existence, since God, exalted is He, knew that they would deny, so He wrote it against them in the Book of Decrees.

*Wa ma wajadna li-aktharihim min 'ahd* (We did not find in most of them any fulfilment of covenant): that is, We did not find that most of them fulfilled the covenants that were taken from them on the day the covenant was taken.

**Meaning of the two verses:**

The Lord, exalted is He, addresses His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) saying: ﴿Those towns—We relate to you some of their news﴾, that is, some of their accounts with their prophets: how their messengers called them to faith, monotheism and obedience; how those nations rejected God's call and were arrogant toward worshipping Him; and how Our judgement was carried out against them, so that perhaps your people might remember, believe and affirm the oneness of God. His saying: ﴿And there had certainly come to them their messengers with clear proofs﴾, that is, with evident arguments for the truthfulness of their call and with what their messengers brought to them of commands and prohibitions from their Lord. His saying: ﴿But they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾, that is, those people of the towns who were destroyed were not going to believe in what they had denied, according to God's knowledge and decree, since God knew that they would not believe, so He wrote this against them, and therefore they do not believe. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of the disbelievers﴾, that is, just as it was written against the destroyed people of the towns that they would not believe, and they indeed did not believe, so He destroyed them, in the same way He seals the hearts of the disbelievers, so they do not believe until the punishment seizes them while they are wrongdoers through their disbelief. This divine judgement rests on the principle that God knew of every human being, before creating him, what he would desire, what he would prefer over others, and what he would do by his own choice and will; so He wrote that for him, and when he comes out into this world he does not act except by it, in order to reach what was written for him, and He decreed it for him from eternity, before the creation of the heavens and the earth. His saying: ﴿And We found for most of them no covenant﴾, that is, We did not find among those nations that We destroyed—the peoples of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb—any fulfilment of the covenant We had taken from them before their creation: faith in Us, worship of Us, obedience to Us and obedience to Our messengers. We found most of them to be none other than defiantly disobedient, departing from Our obedience and the obedience of Our messengers. Thus We brought down upon them Our vengeance and sent down Our punishment, and We destroyed them all.

**Guidance from the two verses:**

1. Confirmation of divine revelation and the affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), because the recounting of the news of earlier peoples is not received except through divine revelation, and it is received from God only by a messenger prepared for that purpose.

2. The presence of clear proofs, however strong and evident, is not sufficient for the faith of one whom God has not willed to guide.

3. The believer is one who believed in eternity, and the disbeliever is one who disbelieved in it.

4. The sealing of the hearts of the disbelievers has as its cause their choosing disbelief, evil and corruption, and their persistence in that whatever the circumstances.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 109–112**

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Sahir 'alim* (a knowing sorcerer): one who has knowledge of sorcery and expertise in it, not merely a claimant.

*Min ardikum* (from your land): from your country, so that he may seize it and rule over you.

*Fama dha ta'murun* (so what do you advise?): advise me on what you see as right in resolving this problem.

*Arjihi* (postpone him): delay him and his brother, and do not hasten against them before taking the necessary precautions.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 113–116:

Explanation of the words:

The sorcerers (al-saharah): plural of sahir (sorcerer), one who has mastered the art of sorcery and affects people's eyes with his sorcery.

Indeed for us there is surely a reward (inna lana la-ajran): that is, a recompense from You, meaning a payment You give us if we prevail.

We are the ones who cast (nahnu al-mulqin): our staffs.

They bewitched the eyes of the people (sahharu a'yun al-nas): where the spectators in the arena came to see the staffs and ropes of sorcery turn, in their sight, into serpents and snakes filling the arena.

And they struck them with terror (wa-istarhabuhum): that is, they put dread and fear into people's hearts because of the strength of the effect of the sorcery on their eyes.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the dialogue taking place between Musa, peace be upon him, on one side, and Pharaoh and his chiefs on the other. The preceding verses stated that the chiefs advised Pharaoh to imprison Musa and his brother Harun and to send police into the cities to bring experts in the art of sorcery to debate Musa, hoping they would overcome him. Indeed Pharaoh sent summoners into his cities to gather the experts in sorcery, and here they had arrived. God the Exalted said: ﴿And the sorcerers came to Pharaoh﴾. They realized that the situation was very difficult for Pharaoh, so they demanded a great reward if they overcame Musa and his brother, and Pharaoh agreed to their request. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And the sorcerers came to Pharaoh; they said, "Indeed for us there is surely a reward if we are the victors." He said, "Yes"﴾. He also added to it that he would make them among his close companions and the men of his palace, so he said: ﴿And indeed you will be among the near ones﴾, that is, near to us. Here they advanced toward Musa, as though confident in their magical strength and that the contest would be theirs. They advanced to cast their magical implements, or Musa advanced upon them. They said: ﴿O Musa, either you cast or we will be the ones who cast﴾, that is, throw your staff, or we will throw ours. Musa said to them: ﴿Throw﴾. So they threw, and in fact they bewitched the eyes of the people and brought a great sorcery, as God the Exalted reported, a matter that struck the spectators with terror, so much so that Musa, peace be upon him, felt fear in himself, and his Lord the Exalted forbade him from that and informed him that he would be the victor by God's permission. This report has come in Surah Taha.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The permissibility of asking for payment for work a person does outside the scope of worship.

2- The permissibility of government promotions for one who has rendered great service to the state.

3- The real effect of sorcery on people's eyes, such that they see a thing contrary to what it is, since the staffs and ropes were transformed in people's eyes into snakes and serpents.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 117–122:

Explanation of the words:

Talqaf (تلقف): takes swiftly and with astonishing dexterity.

Ma ya'fikun (ما يأفكون): what they turn about by their sorcery and deception.

Fawaqa'a al-haqq (فوقع الحق): was established and became manifest.

Saghirin (صاغرين): humiliated.

Sajidin (ساجدين): cast down upon their faces in prostration to their Lord, the Lord of the worlds.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains that of the contest or trial between Musa (peace be upon him) and the sorcerers of Pharaoh. After the sorcerers cast their ropes and staffs into the arena, and by sorcerous deception they became serpents and snakes, and the people were terrified by the scene, and Pharaoh and his chiefs thought they would prevail, Allah the Exalted inspired Musa to cast his staff. He cast it, ﴿and behold, it swallowed up what they had faked﴾, meaning it took it in and devoured it. Thereby ﴿the truth was established﴾, meaning it became manifest, firm and settled, ﴿and what they had been doing was nullified﴾, meaning the sorcery and deception. His words, ﴿So they were overcome﴾, refer to Pharaoh, his chiefs and his people. ﴿There and then﴾, meaning in the arena of the contest and trial, ﴿and they turned back﴾ to their homes, ﴿humbled﴾, meaning abased and defeated.

His words, ﴿And the sorcerers were cast down prostrate﴾, mean that after they witnessed the great sign, it overwhelmed them, so they fell down prostrate as though someone had thrown them onto the ground, unable to move, and they said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun﴾. Included in this is that they rejected the false lordship of Pharaoh, because belief in Allah necessarily entails rejecting whatever is other than Him. For this reason they said ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun﴾, hinting at their disbelief in the tyrant Pharaoh and in every deity other than Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A demonstration of Allah's sunnah (way/law): when truth and falsehood meet in any arena, victory always belongs to the truth.

2- The nullity of sorcery and the failure of its practitioners, based on His words in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿And the sorcerer does not prosper wherever he comes﴾ [Verse 69].

3- The virtue of knowledge and that it is the cause of guidance. The sorcerers' faith was the fruit of knowledge, for they recognized that what Musa brought was not sorcery but a sign from Allah, so they believed.

4- A manifestation of qadar (divine decree): the sorcerers became disbelievers and by evening were Muslims.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains that of the contest or trial between Musa (peace be upon him) and the sorcerers of Pharaoh. After the sorcerers cast their ropes and staffs into the arena, and by sorcerous deception they became serpents and snakes, and the people were terrified by the scene, and Pharaoh and his chiefs thought they would prevail, Allah the Exalted inspired Musa to cast his staff. He cast it, ﴿and behold, it swallowed up what they had faked﴾, meaning it took it in and devoured it. Thereby ﴿the truth was established﴾, meaning it became manifest, firm and settled, ﴿and what they had been doing was nullified﴾, meaning the sorcery and deception. His words, ﴿So they were overcome﴾, refer to Pharaoh, his chiefs and his people. ﴿There and then﴾, meaning in the arena of the contest and trial, ﴿and they turned back﴾ to their homes, ﴿humbled﴾, meaning abased and defeated.

Included in this is that they rejected the false lordship of Pharaoh, because belief in Allah necessarily entails rejecting whatever is other than Him. For this reason they said ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun﴾, hinting at their disbelief in the tyrant Pharaoh and in every deity other than Allah.

4- A manifestation of qadar (divine decree): the sorcerers became disbelievers and by evening were Muslims.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 123–126:

Explanation of the words:

*Amantum bihi* (آمنتم به): That is, you believed him in what he brought and called to.

*Makrun makartumuhu* (مكر مكرتموه): That is, a stratagem you devised and colluded with Musa upon.

*Min khilaf* (من خلاف): By cutting off the right hand and the left foot, or vice versa.

*Thumma la-usallibannakum* (ثم لأصلبنكم): Taslib (crucifixion): binding someone to a piece of wood until death.

*Munqalibun* (منقلبون): That is, returning.

*Wa-ma tanqimu minna* (وما تنقم منا): That is, what you dislike in us and disapprove of in us, except our believing in the signs of our Lord when they came to us.

*Afrigh 'alayna sabran* (أفرغ علينا صبراً): That is, pour upon us a strong patience, so that we may remain steadfast in the face of the punishment Pharaoh has threatened us with, and not revert after our faith.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the events of the stories of Musa and Pharaoh. In the verses before these, the debate between Musa and the magicians took place, with the victory of Musa (peace be upon him) and the disgraceful defeat of Pharaoh, for after the truth became clear and manifest to them, the magicians believed, submitted, and prostrated to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. In these verses, the Exalted informs of Pharaoh's trial of the magicians, saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Pharaoh said﴾, that is, to the magicians, ﴿"You have believed in him"﴾, that is, in Musa, ﴿"before I give you permission"﴾, that is, to believe in him. This is an expression with the scent of defeat and foolishness, for otherwise, can belief be subject to permission or its absence? Belief is an inward submission that has no connection to permission except from Allah, the Exalted. Then he said to them, ﴿"Indeed, this is a scheme you have devised in the city to drive its people out of it"﴾, that is, what you have done in claiming victory over Musa after showing enthusiasm at the start of the contest is nothing but a scheme and a hidden plot arranged between you and Musa in the city before going out to the field of the contest, and its aim is to drive the people out of the city and for you to seize it. Then he threatened and warned them with his saying, ﴿"But you will soon know"﴾ what I will do to you. He mentioned what he had resolved upon, saying, swearing an oath, ﴿"I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides"﴾, meaning from each one of them his right hand and his left foot, then he will crucify them on trunks of wood in a specific place so that they die thus as a deterrent and a lesson to others. This is what Pharaoh declared and made clear to the believing magicians. So what was the answer of the magicians? ﴿They said, "Indeed, to our Lord we are returning"﴾, that is, returning. Your killing us adds nothing but bringing us closer to our Lord and returning us to Him, and we long for meeting our Lord; therefore your judgment to kill us does not harm us. And another thing: ﴿"You take revenge on us"﴾, O Pharaoh, that is, you dislike in us and disapprove of us, not for a crime we committed or corruption in the land we spread, but you only resent in us our believing in the signs of our Lord when they came to us, and this is nothing that brings blame upon us or shame that befalls us. Therefore, ﴿"Decree what you will decree; you only decree concerning this worldly life"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 72]. Then they turned to Allah, raised their hands to Him, and said, humbly and imploringly, ﴿"Our Lord, pour upon us patience"﴾, so that we may bear the punishment for Your sake, ﴿"and take us in death as Muslims"﴾. Pharaoh carried out his crime, but that caused unrest in the land, and neither Pharaoh nor his chiefs had expected it, as the following verses indicate.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Hearts darkened by disbelief and crime, their owners do not refrain from lying and accusing the innocent.

2- The virtue of istirja' (saying ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 156]), for the magicians resorted to it when Pharaoh threatened them, saying ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾, that is, returning, so what they were threatened with became easy for them.

3- The legitimacy of asking Allah for patience in trials in order to remain steadfast in faith.

4- The excellence of dying upon Islam, and that it is a lofty aim for the people of faith.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 127–129:

Explanation of the words:

"Said the chiefs": that is, of Pharaoh.

"Will you leave": that is, will you abandon.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 130–133:

Explanation of the words:

"We afflicted the people of Pharaoh with years (of drought)": that is, We punished them with years of barrenness and famine.

"And a loss of fruits": through calamities that strike them, and through their failing to bear fruit.

"Good (ḥasanah)": whatever brings prosperity, abundance, plentiful provision and well-being.

"Evil (sayyi'ah)": the opposite of good, namely drought, high prices and sickness.

"They ascribe ill omen to Moses (yaṭṭayyarū bi-Mūsā)": that is, they consider Moses and his people to be a bad omen.

"The flood, the locusts, the lice, and the frogs": the flood (ṭūfān) is overwhelming floods; the locust is well known for devouring crops and fruits; the lice (qummal) may be the familiar lice, and may also be weevils in grain; the frogs (ḍafādi') are the plural of ḍafda'ah, an animal found in water and marshes.

"And the blood": blood is well known. It may be a nosebleed or hemorrhage, or the water they drank turning into fresh blood in their vessels and their mouths, a sign for Moses, peace be upon him.

"But they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people": because they did not believe in these signs; that is, they were corrupters, for which reason their destruction was decreed.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Moses and the people of Pharaoh. When Pharaoh and his household witnessed the sign of the staff and the defeat of magic before them, and the sorcerers believed, arrogance drove them to persist in disbelief and obstinacy. The Lord, exalted is He, afflicted them with drought and famine for years, so that they might take heed. But they did not take heed. God did not turn their drought into abundance and their affliction into well-being, so they did not return. In prosperity they said, "This is ours; we deserve it and are worthy of it." In famine and affliction they said, "This comes from the ill omen of Moses and the Children of Israel." God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Surely their omen is with God﴾, because He is the one who manages the affair, the Creator of everything, the One who appoints for good its causes and for evil its causes. But most of them do not know. Therefore they said, "We take ill omen from you, Moses and those with you," and they insisted on disbelief and persisted in denial and obstinacy, until they said to Moses: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not believe you﴾. Had they known, they would not have persisted in disbelief nor said what they said. The causes of good are faith and piety, and the causes of evil are disbelief and sins, since what is meant here by good and evil is goodness and harm.

Here, after this insistence, obstinacy and denial, Moses raised his hands to his Lord, supplicating Him, and said: "My Lord, Your servant Pharaoh has exalted himself in the land, transgressed and become insolent, and his people have broken the covenant. So seize them with a punishment that will be a vengeance upon them, and an admonition for my people, and a sign for those after them." God answered his supplication and sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood. The flood seized them first, and they nearly perished by drowning. They came to Moses and asked him to pray to his Lord to remove this punishment from them, promising that if He removed it they would believe and send the Children of Israel away with him. He prayed to his Lord, and God answered, so they remained in well-being for a month. Then Moses demanded what they had promised him, but they broke their word and persisted in their disbelief. God then sent upon them the locusts, which devoured their crops, trees and fruits, until they cried out and screamed, and came to Moses and gave him their pledge that if God removed this punishment they would believe and send the Children of Israel with him. God removed it from them, and they remained for a period secure from this affliction. Moses again demanded their pledge, and they again broke it. Thus it continued until the five signs were completed, each separated from the next by a period that was short or long. Yet they remained arrogant against faith and obedience, and they were a criminal people, corrupters, with no good in them and no covenant with them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Among God's plan is that He seizes His servants with hardships so that perhaps they will take heed, be admonished and repent.

2- The invalidity of ill omen in every form; rather, misfortune lies in sins, through opposing the law of God, so that calamity and punishment follow from wickedness and disobedience.

3- Ignorance is a cause of disbelief, sins, bad character and corrupt conditions.

4- The failure of the people of Pharaoh to believe despite the signs coming upon them indicates that their faith was not preordained by destiny, and it also indicates that miracles do not necessarily entail faith.

5- Condemnation of criminality, which is the corruption of the soul through polytheism and sins.

"But they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people": because they did not believe in these signs; that is, they were corrupters, for which reason their destruction was decreed.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Moses and the people of Pharaoh. When Pharaoh and his household witnessed the sign of the staff and the defeat of magic before them, and the sorcerers believed, arrogance drove them to persist in disbelief and obstinacy. The Lord, exalted is He, afflicted them with drought and famine for years, so that they might take heed. But they did not take heed. God did not turn their drought into abundance and their affliction into well-being, so they did not return. In prosperity they said, "This is ours; we deserve it and are worthy of it." In famine and affliction they said, "This comes from the ill omen of Moses and the Children of Israel." God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Surely their omen is with God﴾, because He is the one who manages the affair, the Creator of everything, the One who appoints for good its causes and for evil its causes. But most of them do not know. Therefore they said, "We take ill omen from you, Moses and those with you," and they insisted on disbelief and persisted in denial and obstinacy, until they said to Moses: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not believe you﴾. Had they known, they would not have persisted in disbelief nor said what they said. The causes of good are faith and piety, and the causes of evil are disbelief and sins, since what is meant here by good and evil is goodness and harm.

Here, after this insistence, obstinacy and denial, Moses raised his hands to his Lord, supplicating Him, and said: "My Lord, Your servant Pharaoh has exalted himself in the land, transgressed and become insolent, and his people have broken the covenant. So seize them with a punishment that will be a vengeance upon them, and an admonition for my people, and a sign for those after them." God answered his supplication and sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood. The flood seized them first, and they nearly perished by drowning. They came to Moses and asked him to pray to his Lord to remove this punishment from them, promising that if He removed it they would believe and send the Children of Israel away with him. He prayed to his Lord, and God answered, so they remained in well-being for a month. Then Moses demanded what they had promised him, but they broke their word and persisted in their disbelief. God then sent upon them the locusts, which devoured their crops, trees and fruits, until they cried out and screamed, and came to Moses and gave him their pledge that if God removed this punishment they would believe and send the Children of Israel with him. God removed it from them, and they remained for a period secure from this affliction. Moses again demanded their pledge, and they again broke it. Thus it continued until the five signs were completed, each separated from the next by a period that was short or long. Yet they remained arrogant against faith and obedience, and they were a criminal people, corrupters, with no good in them and no covenant with them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Among God's plan is that He seizes His servants with hardships so that perhaps they will take heed, be admonished and repent.

2- The invalidity of ill omen in every form; rather, misfortune lies in sins, through opposing the law of God, so that calamity and punishment follow from wickedness and disobedience.

3- Ignorance is a cause of disbelief, sins, bad character and corrupt conditions.

4- The failure of the people of Pharaoh to believe despite the signs coming upon them indicates that their faith was not preordained by destiny, and it also indicates that miracles do not necessarily entail faith.

5- Condemnation of criminality, which is the corruption of the soul through polytheism and sins.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 134–137:

Explanation of the words:

Ar-rijz (الرجز): the punishment, which is the five mentioned in the aforementioned verse [133].

Ila ajalin hum baligooh idha hum yankuthoon (إلى أجل هم بالغوه إذا هم ينكثون): The meaning of "ajal" (term) is that whenever they asked Musa to supplicate to his Lord to lift the punishment from them, they would promise him faith and the sending of the Children of Israel with him; then Allah would lift the punishment from them. They would remain for a period of time, then Musa would demand of them faith and the sending of the Children of Israel, and they would refuse and break their covenant.

Fa-intaqamna minhum (فانتقمنا منهم): That is, We sent down Our retribution upon them, and drowned them in the yamm (يم), which is the sea.

Alladhina kanoo yustad'afoon (الذين كانوا يستضعفون): They are the Children of Israel.

Mashariq al-ard wa maghariba (مشارق الأرض ومغاربها): They are the land of Egypt and the Levant (ash-Sham).

Wa tammat kalimatu rabbika al-husna (وتمَّت كلمة ربك الحسنى): It is His promise, exalted is He, to them in His saying: ﴿And We wished to show favour to those who were oppressed in the land and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors﴾ [28:5] from Surat al-Qasas.

Wa ma kanoo ya'rishoon (وما كانوا يعرشون): That is, what they raised of buildings of lofty homes and palaces.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Musa with Pharaoh and his people, and these are the final verses of this story. When the punishment (rijz), the detailed torments, befell them: the flood, then the locusts, then the lice, then the frogs, then the blood, they said: ﴿O Musa, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you﴾, meaning to remove the punishment from us if we believe in you and in what you have brought and in what you demand of us, the sending of the Children of Israel with you. They swore and said: ﴿If you remove from us the punishment, we will surely believe in you and send with you the Children of Israel.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when We removed from them the punishment﴾, that is, the torment, ﴿to a term which they were to reach﴾, to a time they would arrive at, ﴿behold, they broke their word﴾ of their covenants; they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel. This occurred between each verse and another until the five verses were completed, and the hour of their destruction drew near. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We drowned them in the yamm﴾, which is the salt sea; that is, He drowned Pharaoh, his army, the men of his state and the nobles of his land. Then the Exalted mentioned the cause of this destruction which befell them, so that it would be a lesson for others, especially the Quraysh, who remained persistent in polytheism and denial, and He said: ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾, as is the case with the Quraysh, the polytheists of the Arabs, and their disbelievers. The Exalted concluded this story, the story of Musa with Pharaoh, with His saying: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts thereof﴾, and they are the Children of Israel, whom the oppressive Pharaoh and his family had enslaved for a long time; ﴿the eastern parts of the land and its western parts﴾, which is the land of Egypt and the Levant, since all of it is what Allah, the Exalted, has blessed; however, the land of the Levant first and then the land of Egypt second, since the Children of Israel entered the land of Palestine after the death of Musa and Harun, when Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua son of Nun) campaigned with them against the Amalekites in the land of Palestine, conquered the lands, and the Children of Israel settled there. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel because of what they endured with patience﴾. The word of Allah meant here is His saying in Surat al-Qasas: ﴿And We wished to show favour to those who were oppressed in the land and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors. And to give them power in the land and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they feared﴾ [28:5–6]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making﴾, of weapons and equipment, sturdy buildings and palaces of lofty construction, ﴿and what they had been building up﴾, raising and elevating lofty structures, and gardens of grapes, bright and flourishing; and He caused their land, their homes and their wealth to be inherited by another people other than them. Allah does what He wills and decrees what He desires. Here ended the story of Musa, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh and his chiefs, and the final outcome was for him, and praise be to Allah.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1. Human weakness appears when affliction descends upon him, when he hastens to Allah, the Exalted, calling upon Him and humbling himself before Him; and when it is lifted, when he forgets what befell him and returns to his habits and what he was upon of polytheism and sins, except one who believes and does righteous deeds, for he exits the circle of weakness, being patient at affliction and thankful at blessings.

2. The cause of punishment in this world and the Hereafter is denial of the signs of Allah by not believing in them and acting upon them, and heedlessness of them, where one neither reflects nor contemplates them and what they were sent down for.

3. Manifestations of Allah's power, the truthfulness of His promise, His great favour upon His creation, and His excellent management of them. Glorified is He, a God who is All-Knowing, All-Wise, Compassionate, Merciful.

**Explanation of the words:**

*"And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea"*: that is, We carried them across until they crossed over to its shore.

*"They were devoted to idols of theirs"*: they would sit before statues of cows carved from stone.

*"Make for us a god"*: that is, an object of worship, as they wanted an image like the ones they had seen.

*"You are a people who are ignorant"*: that is, worship belongs only to Allah, the Exalted.

*"Ruined is what they are engaged in"*: destroyed and lost; it brings them no good and wards off no harm.

*"And when We delivered you"*: that is, remember the blessings of Allah upon you in saving you from the people of Pharaoh.

*"Inflicting on you the worst torment"*: they drive you to the watering places of ruin and destruction through the torment they inflict upon you.

*"A trial from your Lord"*: that is, a severe and grievous test.

**The meaning of the verses:**

This begins a new narrative about the Prophet of Allah, Musa, with his people, the Children of Israel. After the destruction of Pharaoh and his armies in the sea, the account of Musa's call to Pharaoh and his chiefs came to an end. Musa and his brother Harun then faced new problems with their people. After Allah, the Exalted, had brought the Children of Israel across the sea and they had landed safely on its shore, they passed by people devoted to idols of theirs, which were stone cows carved in the form they worshipped, and they were sitting before them in devotion. As soon as the Children of Israel saw these people devoted to the idols, they said to Musa, "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods." This is a statement that shows ignorance of Allah and His signs. Musa, peace be upon him, immediately confronted them with his words: ﴿Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant﴾. He continued to rebuke them and to denounce them severely, saying: ﴿Indeed, these﴾, that is, the people devoted to the idols and those whose condition has deceived you, ﴿are destroyed in what they are engaged in, and worthless is what they have been doing﴾. That is, they and what they are upon are in ruin and loss. Then he said to them, in denial and astonishment: ﴿Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah?﴾, that is, other than my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Shall I seek for you a god to worship besides Allah? What has happened to your minds? He, the Glorified and Exalted, has favoured you over the worlds and honoured you above all the inhabitants of the earth. Is this how you thank Him, by seeking a god other than Him? **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 142–145**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Mīqāt* (appointed time): the set time.

*Akhlufnī fī qawmī* (take my place among my people): be my successor among them.

*Al-mufsidīn* (the corrupters): those who commit sins.

*Istaqarra makānahu* (remained in its place): stood firm and did not move.

*Kharra* (fell): dropped to the ground.

*Afāqa* (came to): the fainting left him and his consciousness returned.

*Iṣṭafaytuka* (I have chosen you): I have selected you.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The narrative continues with the events of Moses and the Children of Israel. After God rescued the Children of Israel from Pharaoh and his chiefs, the incident occurred in which the Children of Israel asked Moses to make for them a god, as the polytheists had gods. Moses informed them of this and reprimanded them for their false statement. God promised Moses that He would speak with him at Mount Tur, and set for him an appointed time at which He would meet him: a month of thirty days, which was the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah, and He added ten to it from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah, so the appointed time was completed as forty nights. When he, peace be upon him, departed, he appointed his brother Harun as his successor among the Children of Israel, instructed him to act righteously, and forbade him to follow the ways of the corrupters. This is the meaning of God's words: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Harun, "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters."﴾ This was so that he might bring the Children of Israel a Book from their Lord containing a complete law by which they would be governed and through which they would be guided, so that they might be perfected and find happiness in it.

God's words ﴿And when Moses came at Our appointed time﴾ mean: at the appointed time We had set and the moment We had determined. His Lord spoke to him without any intermediary between them, so that he heard His speech but did not see His essence. The soul of Moses yearned to see his Lord, so he requested it, saying: ﴿My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You.﴾ His Lord answered him: ﴿You will not see Me﴾, meaning that seeing Me is not possible for you. But if you wish to confirm that seeing Me in this life is not possible, look at the mountain; if it remains in its place after I manifest Myself to it, then you will see Me. ﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell unconscious﴾ upon seeing the mountain, ﴿in a swoon.﴾ That is, he lost consciousness. ﴿When he came to﴾ from the swoon that had overtaken him, ﴿he said, "Glory be to You"﴾, meaning: I declare You free of all imperfection and sanctify You. ﴿I have repented to You﴾, meaning I shall not ask You such a question again. ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾ in You, in Your majesty and Your great dominion. I am Your servant, unable to see You in this abode, the abode of legal obligation and action.

Here his Lord answered him, saying: ﴿O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech, so take what I have given you﴾ of this perfection and great good, ﴿and be among the grateful.﴾ Be thankful to Me for My favors, so that I may increase you, by obeying Me and drawing near to Me by doing what I love and avoiding what I dislike. God's words ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets [an admonition about] everything, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ mean: We wrote for him on his tablets, concerning everything in matters of religion and worldly life, an admonition for his people, consisting of commands, prohibitions, encouragement and warning, and a detailed explanation of everything they need to have explained and clarified. God's words ﴿So take it with strength﴾ mean: We said to him, "Take it with strength," that is, with determination and earnestness, by acting upon its lawful and unlawful matters, both in doing and in refraining. ﴿And command your people﴾ likewise ﴿to take the best of it﴾, that is, the firm obligations it contains, and not the concessions (rukhas), in order to train them and accustom them to bear great burdens, because of the weakness and feebleness that had long afflicted them.

God's words ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾ contain a warning to the Children of Israel against abandoning what came in the tablets of the laws and rulings. For if they abandon all of it or any part of it, they will be considered defiantly disobedient, and for the defiantly disobedient is the Fire of Hell, which is their recompense on the day they meet their Lord. He will show them it. This statement thus carries the utmost threat and warning for those who defy the laws of God by neglecting them and not acting upon them. Let the believers beware of this, for it is a grave matter.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1- Keeping promises is a matter beloved to the Lawgiver (al-Shari'), encouraged by Him, and it is one of the characteristics of the truthful.

2- It is permissible to appoint a successor in the earth for important affairs, let alone for lesser matters.

3- It is legislated to give successors counsel in what is good.

4- It is possible to see God, and this is established in the Hereafter for the people of Paradise.

5- It is impossible to see God in this world, because of human weakness in that regard.

6- The existence of a community receptive to God's rulings preceded the existence of the law that governs it.
