God's words ﴿And when Moses came at Our appointed time﴾ mean: at the appointed time We had set and the moment We had determined. His Lord spoke to him without any intermediary between them, so that he heard His speech but did not see His essence. The soul of Moses yearned to see his Lord, so he requested it, saying: ﴿My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You.﴾ His Lord answered him: ﴿You will not see Me﴾, meaning that seeing Me is not possible for you. But if you wish to confirm that seeing Me in this life is not possible, look at the mountain; if it remains in its place after I manifest Myself to it, then you will see Me. ﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell unconscious﴾ upon seeing the mountain, ﴿in a swoon.﴾ That is, he lost consciousness. ﴿When he came to﴾ from the swoon that had overtaken him, ﴿he said, "Glory be to You"﴾, meaning: I declare You free of all imperfection and sanctify You. ﴿I have repented to You﴾, meaning I shall not ask You such a question again. ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾ in You, in Your majesty and Your great dominion. I am Your servant, unable to see You in this abode, the abode of legal obligation and action.

Here his Lord answered him, saying: ﴿O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech, so take what I have given you﴾ of this perfection and great good, ﴿and be among the grateful.﴾ Be thankful to Me for My favors, so that I may increase you, by obeying Me and drawing near to Me by doing what I love and avoiding what I dislike. God's words ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets [an admonition about] everything, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ mean: We wrote for him on his tablets, concerning everything in matters of religion and worldly life, an admonition for his people, consisting of commands, prohibitions, encouragement and warning, and a detailed explanation of everything they need to have explained and clarified. God's words ﴿So take it with strength﴾ mean: We said to him, "Take it with strength," that is, with determination and earnestness, by acting upon its lawful and unlawful matters, both in doing and in refraining. ﴿And command your people﴾ likewise ﴿to take the best of it﴾, that is, the firm obligations it contains, and not the concessions (rukhas), in order to train them and accustom them to bear great burdens, because of the weakness and feebleness that had long afflicted them.

5- It is impossible to see God in this world, because of human weakness in that regard.

6- The existence of a community receptive to God's rulings preceded the existence of the law that governs it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 146–147:

Explanation of the words:

Sa-asrifu (سأصرف): I will turn away, I will keep away.

Yatakabbarun (يتكبرون): they exalt themselves and act haughtily, so they withhold rights and look down upon people.

Sabil al-rushd (سبيل الرشد): the path of truth, grounded in faith and God-consciousness (taqwa).

Sabil al-ghayy (سبيل الغي): the path of error, grounded in polytheism (shirk) and sins.

Wa kanu 'anha ghafilin (وكانوا عنها غافلين): they do not pay heed to them, do not look into them, and do not reflect on what they indicate and what they guide to.

Habitat a'maluhum (حبطت أعمالهم): their deeds are corrupted so they gain nothing from them, because they are the deeds of a polytheist, and shirk nullifies deeds.

The meaning of the two noble verses:

These two verses contain a sound and correct explanation for every deviation, corruption, injustice and evil that has occurred on earth and will continue to occur until the end of this life. This correct explanation is denial of the signs of God and heedlessness of them. Whether the impetus for denial is arrogance or injustice, imitation or obstinacy, arrogance is nonetheless the strongest of the factors that turn a person away from the signs of God Most High, as His saying, mighty and majestic, at the beginning of the first verse [146] indicates: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who act arrogantly on earth without right﴾. Whoever God turns away, according to His way of turning away His servants, will never accept or return. His saying ﴿And if they see the way of rectitude, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ is an explanation of one of the factors of turning away from the signs of God: that the path of rectitude is presented to the servant and he rejects it, while he sees the path of error and follows it and takes it as his way. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿That is because they denied Our signs﴾ which Our messengers brought ﴿and were heedless of them﴾, not caring about them nor paying attention to them. This is the correct explanation to which we have drawn attention, so let it be pondered. His saying, Exalted is He, in the second verse [147]: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless﴾ is an affirmation of the intended meaning, confirming the loss of those who were turned away from the signs of God Most High, since their deeds were not founded on justice and truth but on injustice and falsehood. Therefore they are void in one respect and do not earn them any good; and in another respect they are evil deeds for which they will be repaid with evil in the abode of recompense, which is the torment of Hellfire. Hence He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾, meaning they are only recompensed for the evil they used to do. And it is part of God's justice, Exalted is He, that whoever brings an evil deed is repaid only with its like, and they will not be wronged.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of God's way regarding the turning away of servants from the signs of God, until they perish as Pharaoh and his people perished.

2- Among the strongest factors of turning away from the signs of God is arrogance.

3- Denial of the signs of God and heedlessness of them are the cause of every error, evil, injustice and corruption.

4- The invalidity of every deed in which its doer did not follow the path of rectitude, which is the path of God, defined and clarified by the Qur'anic signs, and whose markers are raised.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 148–149:

Explanation of the words:

"من حليهم" (min huliyyihim, "from their ornaments"): plural of hilyah (ornaments), which is what a woman adorns herself with for her husband, such as gold bracelets and the like.

"عجلاً جسداً" ('ijlan jasadan, "a calf, a body"): al-'ijl is the young of a cow, and jasad means a real entity, not merely an image on paper or a wall.

"له خوار" (lahu khuwar, "it had a lowing"): al-khuwar is the sound of cattle, as rughā' is the sound of camels.

"ولما سقط في أيديهم" (wa lamma suqita fi aydihim, "and when they were overcome with regret"): meaning they regretted worshipping it, because it was false worship.

Meaning of the verses:

This is a return to the story of Musa (peace be upon him) with his people from the Children of Israel. The context had been with Musa at Mount Tur, when he asked to see Allah and then repented of that. The context then digressed to explain the great principle concerning the cause of the destruction of people and its reason, which is denying the signs of Allah that were revealed and being heedless of them. Then the context returned to the story of Musa with the Children of Israel, and Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the people of Musa took, after him,﴾ that is, after his absence at Mount Tur to converse with his Lord, and in order that he might bring the Book containing the law by which he would govern them and judge them according to its rulings and principles, they took ﴿from their ornaments﴾ that is, the ornaments of their women ﴿a calf, a body having a lowing﴾. This was because al-Samiri asked their women for their ornaments on a flimsy pretext: that these ornaments were borrowed from the women of the Copts and it was not lawful to possess them. He tricked them, and he was a goldsmith, so he melted them down and brought forth for them from it ﴿a calf, a body﴾ that is, a real entity, ﴿having a lowing﴾ that is, a sound like the lowing of cattle. He said to them, "This is your god and the god of Musa, so worship it," but he did not say "and the god of Harun," because Harun was among them as a deputy, so he feared that Harun would deny him, and so he did not attribute it to him. And the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them nor guide them to a way?﴾ is a rebuke and reproach for their dullness and ignorance. How could they believe a god that does not speak to them, nor reason so as to guide them to the path of rectitude if they go astray, and they had indeed gone astray? Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿They took it﴾ that is, as a god ﴿and they were wrongdoers﴾ in that, because Allah, the Lord of Musa and Harun and the worlds, is not a calf, nor a created being of any kind. How ignorant the people were, and how evil their understanding and their state! This is what the first verse [148] indicates. As for the second verse [149], Allah, the Exalted, informed about their state after the matter became clear to them and their error was exposed, and He said: ﴿And when they were overcome with regret﴾ that is, they regretted intensely and saw that by this association they had strayed from the true path and rectitude. They cried out, declaring their repentance: ﴿If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us﴾ that is, this great sin, ﴿we will surely be among the losers﴾ in the Hereafter, and so we will be among the companions of the Hellfire.

Lessons from the two verses:

1- Explanation of one of the laws of the universe: that a person is affected by what he sees and hears, and sight has more effect on the soul than hearing. The Children of Israel, when they saw people pass by a village devoted to idols and asked Musa to make for them a god like them, were the ones who made them accept the calf of al-Samiri that he made for them. For this reason, the sight of things on television and video screens is very influential, and how much it has corrupted minds, polluted souls, and corrupted morals.

2- Condemnation of foolishness and rigidity of thought, as shown by Allah's saying: ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them﴾.

3- When Allah wills good for His servant, He inspires him to repent after sin, so he regrets and seeks forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 150–154:

Explanation of the words:

"Wa lamma raja'a Musa" (And when Musa returned): i.e., from Mount Tur, after more than forty days had passed.

"Asifan" (in anger): i.e., grieved and extremely angry.

"A'jiltum amra rabbikum" (Have you hastened the command of your Lord?): i.e., you hurried ahead of it.

"Bi-ra's akhihi" (by the head of his brother): i.e., Harun, his full brother.

"Qala ibn umm" (He said, "O son of my mother"): its original form is "ya ibn ummi," the yā' was changed to an alif as in "ya ghulaman," and then it was elided. Harun was the full brother of Musa. He addressed him as "son of my mother" because she was the more tender and compassionate.

"Fala tushmit bi al-a'da'" (Do not let the enemies gloat over me): i.e., do not let the enemies rejoice at your humiliating or striking me.

"Ittakhadhu al-'ijl" (They took the calf): i.e., they worshipped it as a god.

"Al-muftarin" (the fabricators): the liars against Allah, the Exalted, by associating partners with Him, i.e., by making a partner for Him.

"Wa lamma sakata 'an Musa al-ghadab" (And when the anger subsided from Musa): his anger departed and his soul was calmed from anxiety and agitation.

"Akhadha al-alwah" (He took up the tablets): i.e., from the ground, after he had cast them down and they had broken.

"Wa fi nuskhatiha" (and in what was copied from them): i.e., in what was copied from them after they were broken, a copy containing guidance and mercy.

"Yarhabun" (fear): they fear their Lord and dread His punishment, so they do not disobey Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the events of the story of Musa with the Children of Israel. In this noble context, Allah, the Exalted, informs that when Musa, peace be upon him, returned to his people from his communion with his Lord, after his Lord had informed him that his people had been tested after him and that the Samiri had led them astray, he returned "angry and grieved," i.e., extremely angry and sorrowful. As soon as he confronted them, he said: "Evil is what you have done in my absence after me! Have you hastened the command of your Lord?" i.e., you hurried and did not complete your Lord's appointment of forty days, so you said Musa has died, and you changed his religion and worshipped the calf. "And he threw down the tablets," i.e., cast them down so that they broke, "and seized his brother by the head," Harun, while his head rebuked him for neglecting the duties of the caliphate. Harun apologized and said: "O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head. I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.'" This is mentioned in Surah Ta-Ha. As for the context here, he said: "Son of my mother, the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies gloat over me, and do not place me among the wrongdoing people," those who did wrong by worshipping the calf. The meaning of "do not let the enemies gloat over me" is: do not harm me with a blow or anything else, for then our enemies, these ignorant wrongdoers, would rejoice. Here Musa felt compassion for him and was tender toward him, and said: "My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful." He sought Allah's favor in accepting his supplication by saying, "You are the Most Merciful of the merciful." This is what the first verse [150] and the second verse [151] contain. As for the third verse, Allah, the Exalted, informs that those who took the calf as a god "will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world." Just as He recompenses them with the wrath that entails punishment and the humiliation that entails disgrace, Allah, the Exalted, recompenses those who fabricate lies against Him by associating partners with Him, while He is free of the partners and the polytheists. This is what the third verse [152] indicates. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 155–157**

**Explanation of the Words:**

**﴿وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوْمَهُ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًا﴾:** i.e., he chose the best of his people, who were seventy men.

**﴿لِمِيقَاتِنَا﴾:** i.e., for the appointed time that We set for him, to come to Us with seventy men.

**﴿أَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾:** the thunderbolt by which hearts trembled.

**﴿السُّفَهَاءُ﴾:** plural of *safih* (foolish), one who has no sound judgment (*rushd*) in all his conduct.

**﴿إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ﴾:** i.e., it is nothing but Your trial, that is, Your test of those among Your servants who are obedient.

**﴿أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنَا﴾:** i.e., You are the one who manages our affairs, and we have no protector other than You.

**﴿هُدْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾:** i.e., we have returned to You and repented.

**﴿الْأُمِّيَّ﴾:** one who can neither read nor write.

**﴿الْمَعْرُوفِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ﴾:** *al-ma'ruf* is what the Shari'ah recognizes as good; *al-munkar* is what the Shari'ah denounces.

**﴿وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبَائِثَ﴾:** i.e., by Allah's leave; *al-khaba'ith* is the plural of *khabithah* (impure things), such as carrion.

**﴿وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ﴾:** *al-isr* means a covenant, and *al-aghlal* means the hardships of the religion.

**﴿عَزَّرُوهُ﴾:** i.e., honored him and revered him.

**﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ﴾:** the Noble Qur'an.

**﴿هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾:** i.e., the successful, the ones saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The context continues with the events concerning Moses and the Children of Israel. After the grave incident that occurred during Moses' absence, namely the worship of the calf by most of the Children of Israel, who took it as a god, Allah the Exalted appointed a time for Moses to come to Him with the best of the Children of Israel, to seek repentance for them from Allah, glorified and exalted is He. Allah says: ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men﴾. When he brought them to Mount Sinai (*Tur*), a cloud overshadowed the mountain, and Moses began to converse with his Lord while they listened. They said to Moses: "We will not believe you until we see Allah plainly," meaning, openly. At this, Allah the Exalted was angered with them, and a blast seized them, causing their hearts and the earth beneath them to tremble, and they all died. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾ [Al-A'raf: 78, 91].

Then Moses (peace be upon him) grieved over the death of the seventy men whom he had chosen as the best, the best among them, and they all died together. So he addressed his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me﴾, that is, before our coming to You, and that was at the place where the Children of Israel had worshipped the calf. ﴿Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?﴾ i.e., because of the deed of the foolish who have no sound judgment, namely those who worshipped the calf, just as those who asked to see Allah did. As for his saying (peace be upon him): ﴿It is nothing but Your trial﴾, i.e., nothing but Your test and affliction, ﴿by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector﴾, so we have no one other than You. ﴿So forgive us﴾, i.e., our sins, ﴿and have mercy upon us﴾ by lifting the punishment from us, ﴿and You are the Best of forgivers﴾. ﴿And decree for us in this world a good﴾ by enabling us to do righteous deeds and accepting them from us, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ by forgiving our sins and admitting us into Your Paradise with the rest of Your righteous servants. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 158–162:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Lā ilāha illā Huwa﴾: that is, there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.

The Ummi Prophet (al-nabī al-ummī): the one who informs about Allah and is informed by Allah, Most High. Ummi means one who could not read or write, ascribed to "umm" (mother), as if he had remained with his mother and had not yet learned.

"Believes in Allah and His words": one who believes in Allah as Lord and God, and in His words, both legislative (tashrī'iyyah) and cosmic, decreed by destiny (kawniyyah qadariyyah).

"That you may be guided" (tahtadūn): that you may be guided to the path of your perfection and happiness in both lives.

"A community that guides by the truth": that is, a group that guides themselves and others by the true religion, and by it they act justly in their judgments, both over themselves and over others, with fairness and equity, without oppression or injustice.

Asbāṭan (tribes): plural of sibt, which in Arabic means tribe.

"His people asked him for water" (istasqāhu qawmuhu): that is, they asked him for water because of their thirst.

Fa-nbajasat: then gushed forth (fa-nfajarat).

Al-manna wa al-salwā: al-manna is a sweet substance like honey that descended upon the leaves of trees; al-salwā is a delicious bird whose meat is tasty.

"Dwell in this town" (uskunū hādhihi al-qaryah): it refers to the capital of Palestine.

"And [say] ḥiṭṭah": that is, "Remove from us our sins," meaning an announcement of their repentance.

Rijzan min al-samā' (a punishment from the heaven): that is, a punishment from Allah, Most High.

Meaning of the verses:

After praising the Ummi Prophet and his community, and restricting success in both abodes to those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him, one might suppose that this Prophet, like the other prophets before him, is a prophet to his own people only, and that the perfection mentioned does not extend beyond his people. This misconception is removed by this verse [158], in which Allah commanded His Messenger to announce the universality of his mission in a manner that leaves no room for doubt, so He said: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾. His saying ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ is a description of Allah, and His saying ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾ is an affirmation of Allah's divinity after mentioning His power, sovereignty, dominion and governance; therefore it is necessary that there be no worshipped one except Him, and this is so, for every other object of worship is worshipped out of ignorance, obstinacy and wrongdoing. His saying ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the Ummi Prophet﴾ is a command from the True God to all people to believe in Him as Lord and God, and in His Messenger, the Ummi Prophet, as Prophet and Messenger. His saying ﴿who believes in Allah and His words﴾ is a description of the Ummi Prophet, for among the attributes of the Ummi Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), is that he believes in Allah with the truest and most complete belief, and believes in His words, that is, the words of the Lord, both legislative, which are the verses of the noble Qur'an, and cosmic, by which Allah brings into being whatever He wills of existing things, for by them He says to a thing "Be," and it is, as He said regarding Jesus with that word "Be," and he was ('Īsā, peace be upon him). His saying ﴿and follow him, that you may be guided﴾ is the command of Allah to all people, after the command to believe in Him and in His Ummi Prophet Messenger, a command to follow His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in hope that whoever follows him in what he brought will be guided to the path of success in both abodes. This is what the first verse [158] contains.

As for the second verse [159], it contains the divine information that the people of Moses, even though they went astray, committed sin and transgressed, that does not mean there were not among them or between them those who were upon the guidance of Allah. This verse came as a safeguard against such an understanding, for Allah, Most High, informed that ﴿Among the people of Moses is a community﴾, that is, a group, whether large or small, ﴿who guide by the truth﴾, that is, who act upon the truth in their beliefs and worship, call to it, and by the truth act justly between themselves and others; they live by fairness and justice. Allah, Most High, did not mention where they were or when they existed, so that is not to be investigated, for there is no benefit in it. Then the context returned to the people of Moses, mentioning their events as an admonition and lesson, and affirming the truth of the oneness of Allah, Most High, establishing the prophethood of His Messenger, and affirming the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, or the Last Day. Allah, Most High, said in the third verse [160]: ﴿And We divided them﴾, that is, the Children of Israel, ﴿into twelve tribes, as communities﴾. The original meaning of sibt is a grandson through a daughter, and it is intended here to mean the descendants of each tribe from the sons of Jacob, peace be upon him. So the tribes among the Children of Israel are like the clans among the Arabs, each clan being traced to its first father. The word "twelve" is feminine because asbāṭ means factions, and faction (firqah) is feminine. His saying: ﴿And We inspired to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾, that is, We informed him by way of revelation, which is a hidden, swift notification. The meaning of "istasqāhu" is that they asked him for water because they were thirsty due to the scarcity of water in the desert of Sinai.

﴿That strike the rock with your staff﴾: this is what was revealed, and he struck, ﴿so there gushed forth﴾, that is, burst forth, ﴿from it twelve springs﴾, so that each tribe might drink from its own particular spring, so that no collision or crowding would occur that would result in harm. His saying, Most High, ﴿Every people had known their drinking place﴾, means that each group knew its own particular water. His saying, Most High, ﴿And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them al-manna and al-salwā﴾ is a mention of Allah's favour upon the Children of Israel while they were in the company of Moses and Aaron during the incident of the wandering (al-tīh), where Allah, Most High, sent the clouds, which is white cool clouds shading them from the sun so that it would not scorch them, and sent down upon them al-manna, which is a sweet substance like honey that fell at night like dew upon the trees, and subjected for them a bird of delicious meat called al-salwā, which is the well-known quail bird, and We said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾. His saying, Most High, ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾ refers to their rebellion against their prophets and their disobedience to their Lord until there descended upon them what descended of affliction: ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾. This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third verse [161], it contains an incident after the events of the wandering in the desert of Sinai, namely that Joshua son of Nun, after he assumed the leadership of the Children of Israel following the death of Moses and Aaron and the end of the period of wandering, which was forty years, fought with the Children of Israel against the Amalekites in the land of al-Quds, and Allah granted him victory. He said to the Children of Israel: "Enter the gate of the city prostrating", that is, bowing in humility to Allah and in gratitude for the blessing of conquest after victory and deliverance from the wandering. And [He said], during your entry through the gate, say the word "ḥiṭṭah", which indicates your repentance and your seeking forgiveness from your Lord for your sins; indeed Allah will forgive you your errors, and He will increase the good-doers among you in bounty and abundant goodness, along with His pleasure with you and your admission into Paradise. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Most High: ﴿And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this town"﴾, that is, the city of Palestine, ﴿and eat from it wherever you wish﴾, because of its bounties, ﴿and say, "Ḥiṭṭah," and enter the gate prostrating; We will forgive you your sins, and We will increase the good-doers.﴾

As for the fourth verse [162], it contains information about those among the Children of Israel who did wrong, those who were commanded to enter the town and enter the gate prostrating. They changed ﴿a word other than that which had been said to them﴾: instead of "ḥiṭṭah" they said "ḥinṭah" (wheat), and instead of entering bowing and prostrating, they entered crawling on their buttocks. When Allah, Most High, saw that rebellion, disobedience and lack of gratitude, He sent down upon them a plague from the sky that nearly destroyed the last of them. After praising the Ummi Prophet and his community, and restricting success in both abodes to those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him, one might suppose that this Prophet, like the other prophets before him, is a prophet to his own people only, and that the perfection mentioned does not extend beyond his people. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 158–162:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Lā ilāha illā Huwa﴾: that is, there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.

The Ummi Prophet (al-nabī al-ummī): the one who informs about Allah and is informed by Allah, Most High. Ummi means one who could not read or write, ascribed to "umm" (mother), as if he had remained with his mother and had not yet learned.

"Believes in Allah and His words": one who believes in Allah as Lord and God, and in His words, both legislative (tashrī'iyyah) and cosmic, decreed by destiny (kawniyyah qadariyyah).

"That you may be guided" (tahtadūn): that you may be guided to the path of your perfection and happiness in both lives.

"A community that guides by the truth": that is, a group that guides themselves and others by the true religion, and by it they act justly in their judgments, both over themselves and over others, with fairness and equity, without oppression or injustice.

Asbāṭan (tribes): plural of sibt, which in Arabic means tribe.

"His people asked him for water" (istasqāhu qawmuhu): that is, they asked him for water because of their thirst.

Fa-nbajasat: then gushed forth (fa-nfajarat).

Al-manna wa al-salwā: al-manna is a sweet substance like honey that descended upon the leaves of trees; al-salwā is a delicious bird whose meat is tasty.

"Dwell in this town" (uskunū hādhihi al-qaryah): it refers to the capital of Palestine.

"And [say] ḥiṭṭah": that is, "Remove from us our sins," meaning an announcement of their repentance.

Rijzan min al-samā' (a punishment from the heaven): that is, a punishment from Allah, Most High.

Meaning of the verses:

After praising the Ummi Prophet and his community, and restricting success in both abodes to those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him, one might suppose that this Prophet, like the other prophets before him, is a prophet to his own people only, and that the perfection mentioned does not extend beyond his people. This misconception is removed by this verse [158], in which Allah commanded His Messenger to announce the universality of his mission in a manner that leaves no room for doubt, so He said: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾. His saying ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ is a description of Allah, and His saying ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾ is an affirmation of Allah's divinity after mentioning His power, sovereignty, dominion and governance; therefore it is necessary that there be no worshipped one except Him, and this is so, for every other object of worship is worshipped out of ignorance, obstinacy and wrongdoing. His saying ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the Ummi Prophet﴾ is a command from the True God to all people to believe in Him as Lord and God, and in His Messenger, the Ummi Prophet, as Prophet and Messenger. His saying ﴿who believes in Allah and His words﴾ is a description of the Ummi Prophet, for among the attributes of the Ummi Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), is that he believes in Allah with the truest and most complete belief, and believes in His words, that is, the words of the Lord, both legislative, which are the verses of the noble Qur'an, and cosmic, by which Allah brings into being whatever He wills of existing things, for by them He says to a thing "Be," and it is, as He said regarding Jesus with that word "Be," and he was ('Īsā, peace be upon him). His saying ﴿and follow him, that you may be guided﴾ is the command of Allah to all people, after the command to believe in Him and in His Ummi Prophet Messenger, a command to follow His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in hope that whoever follows him in what he brought will be guided to the path of success in both abodes. This is what the first verse [158] contains.

As for the second verse [159], it contains the divine information that the people of Moses, even though they went astray, committed sin and transgressed, that does not mean there were not among them or between them those who were upon the guidance of Allah. This verse came as a safeguard against such an understanding, for Allah, Most High, informed that ﴿Among the people of Moses is a community﴾, that is, a group, whether large or small, ﴿who guide by the truth﴾, that is, who act upon the truth in their beliefs and worship, call to it, and by the truth act justly between themselves and others; they live by fairness and justice. Allah, Most High, did not mention where they were or when they existed, so that is not to be investigated, for there is no benefit in it. Then the context returned to the people of Moses, mentioning their events as an admonition and lesson, and affirming the truth of the oneness of Allah, Most High, establishing the prophethood of His Messenger, and affirming the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, or the Last Day. Allah, Most High, said in the third verse [160]: ﴿And We divided them﴾, that is, the Children of Israel, ﴿into twelve tribes, as communities﴾. The original meaning of sibt is a grandson through a daughter, and it is intended here to mean the descendants of each tribe from the sons of Jacob, peace be upon him. So the tribes among the Children of Israel are like the clans among the Arabs, each clan being traced to its first father. The word "twelve" is feminine because asbāṭ means factions, and faction (firqah) is feminine. His saying: ﴿And We inspired to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾, that is, We informed him by way of revelation, which is a hidden, swift notification. The meaning of "istasqāhu" is that they asked him for water because they were thirsty due to the scarcity of water in the desert of Sinai.

﴿That strike the rock with your staff﴾: this is what was revealed, and he struck, ﴿so there gushed forth﴾, that is, burst forth, ﴿from it twelve springs﴾, so that each tribe might drink from its own particular spring, so that no collision or crowding would occur that would result in harm. His saying, Most High, ﴿Every people had known their drinking place﴾, means that each group knew its own particular water. His saying, Most High, ﴿And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them al-manna and al-salwā﴾ is a mention of Allah's favour upon the Children of Israel while they were in the company of Moses and Aaron during the incident of the wandering (al-tīh), where Allah, Most High, sent the clouds, which is white cool clouds shading them from the sun so that it would not scorch them, and sent down upon them al-manna, which is a sweet substance like honey that fell at night like dew upon the trees, and subjected for them a bird of delicious meat called al-salwā, which is the well-known quail bird, and We said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾. His saying, Most High, ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾ refers to their rebellion against their prophets and their disobedience to their Lord until there descended upon them what descended of affliction: ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾. This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third verse [161], it contains an incident after the events of the wandering in the desert of Sinai, namely that Joshua son of Nun, after he assumed the leadership of the Children of Israel following the death of Moses and Aaron and the end of the period of wandering, which was forty years, fought with the Children of Israel against the Amalekites in the land of al-Quds, and Allah granted him victory. He said to the Children of Israel: "Enter the gate of the city prostrating", that is, bowing in humility to Allah and in gratitude for the blessing of conquest after victory and deliverance from the wandering. And [He said], during your entry through the gate, say the word "ḥiṭṭah", which indicates your repentance and your seeking forgiveness from your Lord for your sins; indeed Allah will forgive you your errors, and He will increase the good-doers among you in bounty and abundant goodness, along with His pleasure with you and your admission into Paradise. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Most High: ﴿And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this town"﴾, that is, the city of Palestine, ﴿and eat from it wherever you wish﴾, because of its bounties, ﴿and say, "Ḥiṭṭah," and enter the gate prostrating; We will forgive you your sins, and We will increase the good-doers.﴾

As for the fourth verse [162], it contains information about those among the Children of Israel who did wrong, those who were commanded to enter the town and enter the gate prostrating. They changed ﴿a word other than that which had been said to them﴾: instead of "ḥiṭṭah" they said "ḥinṭah" (wheat), and instead of entering bowing and prostrating, they entered crawling on their buttocks. When Allah, Most High, saw that rebellion, disobedience and lack of gratitude, He sent down upon them a plague from the sky that nearly destroyed the last of them. This is the meaning of His saying, Most High: ﴿So those who did wrong among them changed the word from that which had been said to them, so We sent down upon them a punishment from the sky because they had been wronging.﴾

Lessons from the verses:

1- The universality of the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to all people, Arab and non-Arab, white and yellow.

2- The guidance of a person, whether an individual, a group or a nation, to perfection and happiness depends on following the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

3- The Qur'an's fairness toward nations and communities: it declared that among the Children of Israel there was a community standing upon the truth, after the corruption of the Children of Israel and before the advent of the final Prophet. After the Muhammadan mission, however, no one remains upon the truth except those who believed in him and followed him, since his law abrogates all other laws (naskh).

4- When Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant or a nation and they do not thank for it, it is taken away from them, whether they like it or not, and whoever they may be.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 163–166:

Explanation of the words:

Hadirat al-bahr (حاضرة البحر): i.e., on its shore; it is a town among the towns of the land of al-Quds (Jerusalem).

Ya'dunna fi al-sabt (يمدون في السبت): i.e., they transgress, by hunting during it, which was forbidden to them.

Yawm sabtihim (يوم سبتهم): i.e., the day of their rest from worldly labour, which is Saturday.

Shur'an (شرعاً): plural of shari', meaning apparent and prominent, enticing them by their own presence.

Kadhalika nablu-hum (كذلك نبلوهم): i.e., We test them and try them.

Bima kanu yafsuqun (بما كانوا يفسقون): i.e., because of the defiance they openly displayed, which is disobedience.

Ma'dhiratan ila rabbikum (معذرة إلى ربكم): i.e., We forbid them; if they desist, well and good, but if not, our forbidding will serve as an excuse for us before our Lord.

Falamma nasu ma dhukkiru bihi (فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به): i.e., they neglected and abandoned it, so they did not carry out what they were commanded nor refrain from what they were forbidden.

Al-su' (عن السوء): al-su' is everything that harms the self, from all sins and transgressions.

Bi'adhab ba'is (بعذاب بئيس): i.e., possessing severe might.

Falamma 'ataw 'amma nuhu 'anhu (فلما عتوا عما نهوا عنه): i.e., they became arrogant and defiant, and cared nothing for the prohibition.

Qiradatan khasi'in (قردة خاسئين): qiradah is the plural of qird, the known animal; khasi'in means humiliated and despised, abject.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains concerning the Children of Israel, but here it also concerns the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Jews of Madinah. Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him): ask them, i.e., the Jews, ﴿about the town that was by the sea﴾, i.e., near it, on its shore, and it is a town among the towns of the land of al-Quds and al-Sham; that is, ask them about its people, how the end of their affair turned out: they were transformed into apes and swine as a recompense for their defiance of their Lord's command. He then detailed the event for the sake of lesson and admonition, saying ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, i.e., they exceeded what was permitted to them into what was forbidden to them. They were permitted to hunt whatever they wished except on Saturday, for it is a day of worship, not a day of play, hunting and merriment. ﴿When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, openly on the surface of the water﴾, i.e., enticing them by their own presence, ﴿and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, i.e., during the rest of the days of the week. Thus they were being tested. Allah the Exalted said ﴿thus﴾, i.e., like this trial and test, ﴿We tested them for what they used to defy﴾, i.e., because of their defiance of the obedience to their Lord and His messengers, for there is no disobedience except through a sin; such is the way of Allah the Exalted with people. This is what the first verse [163] contains, which is His saying: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath they did not come to them. Thus We tested them for what they used to defy.﴾

As for the second verse [164], Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger: mention to them also, when a group among them, i.e., among the people of the town, said to another group that was admonishing those who transgressed on the Sabbath, that is, forbidding them from it because it is disobedience, and warning them of the consequence of transgressing against the law of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ This statement from this group indicates their despair of their brethren returning from their defiance and falsehood. The admonishing group answered them: ﴿As an excuse before your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him﴾, i.e., our admonishing them is an excuse for us before Allah on one hand, and on the other hand ﴿perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they repent and abandon this transgression. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ and were warned against, namely Allah's prohibition to them of hunting on Saturday. The meaning of "forgot" is that they abandoned it, paid no attention to their brethren's admonition, and continued their transgression and defiance. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We rescued those who forbade evil﴾, and they are the admonishers among them, and those who grew weary and despaired and so abandoned their admonition, as well as those who persisted in forbidding and admonishing. ﴿And We seized those who did wrong with a severe punishment﴾, i.e., severe in its might, ﴿because they used to defy﴾ the obedience of Allah their Lord. Then Allah the Exalted said to them: ﴿Be apes, despised and humiliated﴾, so they became apes, humiliated, abject and despised. Then they did not remain in their transformed state for more than three days before they died.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The confirmation of revelation and prophethood for the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), since such a narrative recounted to the Children of Israel could only be attained through revelation; otherwise, how would he have known it and related it to the Jews, his companions and family, when a long time had passed since it occurred?

2- When Allah bestows a blessing upon a nation and it then turns away from giving thanks for it, it is exposed to trial first and then to punishment second.

3- The benefit of enjoining good and forbidding evil: Allah the Exalted rescued those who forbade evil and destroyed those who engaged in it and did not desist from it, and not others.

4- The application of the word "evil" (al-su') to disobedience indicates that disobedience, however minor, produces harm in the soul of its doer.

Bima kanu yafsuqun (بما كانوا يفسقون): i.e., because of the defiance they openly displayed, which is disobedience.

Ma'dhiratan ila rabbikum (معذرة إلى ربكم): i.e., We forbid them; if they desist, well and good, but if not, our forbidding will serve as an excuse for us before our Lord.

Falamma nasu ma dhukkiru bihi (فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به): i.e., they neglected and abandoned it, so they did not carry out what they were commanded nor refrain from what they were forbidden.

Al-su' (عن السوء): al-su' is everything that harms the self, from all sins and transgressions.

Bi'adhab ba'is (بعذاب بئيس): i.e., possessing severe might.

Falamma 'ataw 'amma nuhu 'anhu (فلما عتوا عما نهوا عنه): i.e., they became arrogant and defiant, and cared nothing for the prohibition.

Qiradatan khasi'in (قردة خاسئين): qiradah is the plural of qird, the known animal; khasi'in means humiliated and despised, abject.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains concerning the Children of Israel, but here it also concerns the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Jews of Madinah. Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him): ask them, i.e., the Jews, ﴿about the town that was by the sea﴾, i.e., near it, on its shore, and it is a town among the towns of the land of al-Quds and al-Sham; that is, ask them about its people, how the end of their affair turned out: they were transformed into apes and swine as a recompense for their defiance of their Lord's command. He then detailed the event for the sake of lesson and admonition, saying ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, i.e., they exceeded what was permitted to them into what was forbidden to them. They were permitted to hunt whatever they wished except on Saturday, for it is a day of worship, not a day of play, hunting and merriment. ﴿When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, openly on the surface of the water﴾, i.e., enticing them by their own presence, ﴿and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾, i.e., during the rest of the days of the week. Thus they were being tested. Allah the Exalted said ﴿thus﴾, i.e., like this trial and test, ﴿We tested them for what they used to defy﴾, i.e., because of their defiance of the obedience to their Lord and His messengers, for there is no disobedience except through a sin; such is the way of Allah the Exalted with people. This is what the first verse [163] contains, which is His saying: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and on the day they did not keep the Sabbath they did not come to them. Thus We tested them for what they used to defy.﴾

As for the second verse [164], Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger: mention to them also, when a group among them, i.e., among the people of the town, said to another group that was admonishing those who transgressed on the Sabbath, that is, forbidding them from it because it is disobedience, and warning them of the consequence of transgressing against the law of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ This statement from this group indicates their despair of their brethren returning from their defiance and falsehood. The admonishing group answered them: ﴿As an excuse before your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him﴾, i.e., our admonishing them is an excuse for us before Allah on one hand, and on the other hand ﴿perhaps they will fear Him﴾, so that they repent and abandon this transgression. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ and were warned against, namely Allah's prohibition to them of hunting on Saturday. The meaning of "forgot" is that they abandoned it, paid no attention to their brethren's admonition, and continued their transgression and defiance. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We rescued those who forbade evil﴾, and they are the admonishers among them, and those who grew weary and despaired and so abandoned their admonition, as well as those who persisted in forbidding and admonishing. ﴿And We seized those who did wrong with a severe punishment﴾, i.e., severe in its might, ﴿because they used to defy﴾ the obedience of Allah their Lord. Then Allah the Exalted said to them: ﴿Be apes, despised and humiliated﴾, so they became apes, humiliated, abject and despised. Then they did not remain in their transformed state for more than three days before they died.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The confirmation of revelation and prophethood for the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), since such a narrative recounted to the Children of Israel could only be attained through revelation; otherwise, how would he have known it and related it to the Jews, his companions and family, when a long time had passed since it occurred?

2- When Allah bestows a blessing upon a nation and it then turns away from giving thanks for it, it is exposed to trial first and then to punishment second.

3- The benefit of enjoining good and forbidding evil: Allah the Exalted rescued those who forbade evil and destroyed those who engaged in it and did not desist from it, and not others.

4- The application of the word "evil" (al-su') to disobedience indicates that disobedience, however minor, produces harm in the soul of its doer.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 167–170**

**Explanation of the words (شرح الكلمات):**

**Ta'adhdhana** (تأذن): He declared and proclaimed.

**La-yab'athanna** (ليبعثن): That He would surely empower [someone] over them.

**Man yasumuhum su'a al-'adhab** (من يسومهم سوء العذاب): That is, He would make them taste and would subject them to the worst torment, such as humiliation and destitution.

**Waqatta'nahum** (وقطعناهم): That is, We divided them into separate groups.

**Balawnahum bil-hasanat wal-sayyi'at** (بلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات): We tested them with good and evil, or with blessings and calamities.

**Fakhalafa min ba'dihim khalf** (فخلف من بعدهم خلف): The word *khalf* with a sukun on the lam means a bad successor, while *khalf* with a fatha on the lam means a good successor.

**Warithu al-kitab** (ورثوا الكتاب): That is, the Torah.

**'Arada hadha al-adna** (عرض هذا الأدنى): That is, the perishable trappings of this world, namely wealth.

**Yumassikuna bil-kitab** (يمسكون بالكتاب): That is, they hold fast to what is in the Torah, so they make lawful what God has made lawful in it and make unlawful what He has made unlawful.

**The meaning of the verses (معنى الآيات):**

The context still concerns the Jews. God commanded His Messenger to mention that He had proclaimed that, with absolute certainty, He would empower over the Jews, until the Day of Resurrection, someone who would humiliate and oppress them. This was a punishment from Him for the corruption of their inner intentions and the evil of their deeds. This absolute threat is restricted by one of two conditions. The first is the repentance of those among them who repent, and God's words at the end of this verse indicate this restriction: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning, toward whoever repents. The second is a strong state under whose protection they live. This is the implication of God's words in Surah Al 'Imran: ﴿They are struck with humiliation wherever they are found, except under a rope from Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 112], which is Islam, ﴿and a rope from the people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 112], which is what we mentioned just above. This is what the first verse in this context indicates [167], which is God's words: ﴿And [mention] when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would subject them to the worst torment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

As for the second verse [168], it contains an explanation of God's favour upon the Jews: God dispersed them throughout the earth in separate groups. Among them were the righteous, and among them were others than that. He tested them with good, which is blessings, and with evil, which is calamities, as a preparation for them and a readiness for repentance, if they chose repentance over persistence in crime, wickedness and corruption. This is what the second verse contains, which is God's words: ﴿And We divided them throughout the earth into nations. Among them are the righteous, and among them are others than that. And We tested them with good and evil that perhaps they would return﴾.

As for the third verse [169], God informed that after that community there came a bad successor who inherited the Book, which is the Torah. They inherited it from their predecessors, yet they did not abide by the covenants taken from them within it, despite their reading of it. They preferred the world over the Hereafter, so they permitted usury, bribery and the other forbidden things. They claimed that they would be forgiven, and whenever unlawful wealth came to them, they took it and deluded themselves with forgiveness, lying against God. God said, rebuking them: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth?﴾ They had read this in the Book and understood it, yet despite this they dared against God and lied about Him, claiming that He would forgive them. Then God addresses them directly, reminding and admonishing them, saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not reason?﴾

In the fourth verse in this context, God opens the door of hope for them, saying: ﴿And those who hold firmly to the Book﴾, that is, who act with diligence and earnestness upon what it contains of rulings and laws, and who do not neglect any part of that, ﴿and establish prayer, indeed We do not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers﴾. The meaning of this is that they are reformers if they hold fast to the Book and establish prayer, and that God will reward them for their reform of themselves and others with the greatest and most complete reward, because He does not let the reward of the reformers be lost.

**Guidance from the verses (هداية الآيات):**

1. A brief account of the history of the Jews in these four verses.
2. Among the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) are the righteous, and among them are others than that.
3. Condemnation of preferring the world over the Hereafter, and of wishing for forgiveness while persisting in crime.
4. The Hereafter is better than this world for the God-fearing.
5. Encouragement to hold fast to the Book by reading it, learning it, and acting upon it, making lawful what it makes lawful and unlawful what it makes unlawful.
6. The virtue of establishing prayer.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, Verses 171–174**

**Explanation of Key Words:**

*Wa-idh nataqna al-jabal*: We raised the mountain from its base above their heads.

*Waqi' bihim*: It fell upon them.

*Khudhu ma ataynakum bi-quwwah*: Commit yourselves firmly to carrying out what was enjoined upon you of the rulings of the Torah, with resolve.

*Wa-dhkuru ma fihi*: Do not forget what you committed yourselves to, namely rising to uphold the rulings of the Torah.

*Min zuhurihim dhurriyyatahum*: He took their descendants from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, at the place Nu'man, in 'Arafat.

*Ashhadahum 'ala anfusihim*: That He, the Exalted, is their Lord and their God, and that they have no lord besides Him and no god besides Him.

*Al-mubtilun*: Those who practise *shirk* (associating partners with God) and sins, for all of these are falsehood (*batil*) in which there is no truth.

*Nufassil al-ayat*: We make the signs clear and explicit by varying the methods of address, repeating proofs, coining parables, and recounting stories.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The first verse in this context concludes the discourse addressed to the Jews, for the Exalted said to His Messenger: ﴿And [remember] when We raised the mountain above them as though it were a canopy﴾. That is, O Messenger, recount to them when We *nataqna*, i.e., lifted above them the mountain of Tur from its base, so that it became above them like a canopy. ﴿And they thought that it would fall upon them﴾, i.e., that it would collapse upon them. And We said to them: ﴿Take what We have given you with resolve﴾. What is meant by what He gave them is the rulings of the Torah and the laws it contains, and taking it means acting upon it and committing oneself to all that it commands and forbids. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And remember what is in it﴾, means: remember what is in what We have given you of commands and prohibitions, and do not forget it, for remembering it is what prepares you to act upon it, and thereby the fear of God, the Mighty and Majestic, is attained for you. This is what the first verse indicates, and it is the conclusion of the discourse about the Jews.

As for the second verse [172], which is His saying: ﴿And [remember] when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾, it is an event worthy of mention and attention because of the lesson it contains. God, the Exalted, brought forth from the backbone of Adam his descendants, and endowed them with speech by His power, which nothing can overcome. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 175–178:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Wa-otlu 'alayhim naba'* (وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ): Recite to them.

*Fa-nsalakha minha* (فَانسَلَخَ مِنْهَا): He disbelieved in them, abandoned them, and cast them behind his back, moving far away from them.

*Fa-atba'ahu al-shaytan* (فَأَتْبَعَهُ الشَّيْطَانُ): He caught up with him and overtook him.

*Min al-ghawin* (مِنَ الْغَاوِينَ): Among the astray, the misguided and the lost, who are not rightly guided and will not be saved.

*Akhlada ila al-ardh* (أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الأَرْضِ): He inclined to the world, relied upon it, and had no concern except the world.

*Yalhathu* (يَلْهَثُ): *Al-lahath* is heavy breathing with the tongue hanging out, from fatigue and exhaustion.

*Sa'a* (سَاءَ): Evil, ugly.

*Mathalan* (مَثَلاً): That is, a description or example.

**Meaning of the verses:**

God says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And recite to them﴾, that is, recite to your people and to everyone among mankind who receives this Book, ﴿the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾, that is, the story of the man to whom We gave Our signs, which contain the proofs, arguments, laws, rulings and moral teachings, but he abandoned them and moved away from them. He did not recite them, did not reflect upon them, and did not act by them, neither by way of reasoning nor by way of application (*tatbiq*). ﴿So Satan overtook him﴾, that is, he caught up with him and gained power over him, namely Iblis, because by his abandoning of the signs, Satan found a way to him. ﴿And he became among the astray﴾, that is, among the misguided, corrupt and lost. ﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾, that is, through the signs, to the heights of glory and perfection, and to the lofty ranks in the Hereafter. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾, that is, he inclined toward it and relied upon it, and he devoted himself to desires and extravagance in pleasures, having no concern except to obtain them. ﴿And he followed his desire﴾, abandoning his reason and the revelation of his Lord which was before him. So he became like the example that fits him, ﴿like the example of the dog﴾, that is, in panting and exhaustion, in dependence, and in lacking self-direction. ﴿If you drive him away, he pants; or if you leave him, he pants﴾. His confusion and fatigue never cease.

As for His saying, ﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾, that is, this parable which We have set forth for that man to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, and what happened to him, which We have related to you, is the example of the people who denied Our signs at every time and place. Accordingly, ﴿So relate the stories﴾, O Our Messenger, ﴿that they may reflect﴾, that is, so that perhaps the Quraysh will reflect, take heed, and return to the truth, and thus be perfected and made happy.

As for His saying, ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and were wronging themselves﴾, that is, evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and rejected them, so that they did not affirm the oneness of God, the Exalted, nor submitted to Him. ﴿And they were wronging themselves﴾ by defiling themselves with the traces of polytheism and sins.

As for His saying, ﴿Whomever God guides, he is the one guided﴾, that is, whoever God has granted success in guidance, so that he believed, submitted, and remained steadfast upon the path of truth, he is truly the one guided. And whomever God forsakes, because of his intense turning away from the truth and his arrogance toward it, he is lost; so those are the losers, the manifest loss.

1. The gravity of this account which God commanded His Messenger to recite to people.

2. Abandoning the noble Qur'an by not reciting it, not reflecting upon it, and not acting by it leads the servant to become the subject of this verse. First, Satan gains power over him, so he becomes one of the deviators; second, he clings to the earth, as is the state of many, so that none of them has any concern except the world.

Then he follows his desire rather than his reason or the law of God. Thereupon he becomes the likeness of a dog that pants, whose confusion and following of others never end, exactly like the dog. This is the state of those who turn away from the Book of God, in this verse, so let the intelligent person reflect upon it.

3. There is no elevation, no sovereignty, and no perfection except by acting upon the Qur'an. It is what elevates, as in His saying, ﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾, that is, through the signs from which he detached himself, God forbid.

4. Guidance is in the hand of God. Whoever desires it should seek it from God with sincerity of heart and purity of intention, for God does not deprive him of it. Whoever turns away from God, God turns away from him.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 179–181:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Dharána li-Jahannam* (ذرأنا لجهنم): We created for Hell, meaning for punishment therein and for abiding in it.

*Lā yafqahūna bihā* (لا يفقهون بها): The words of Allah and the words of His Messenger.

*Lā yubṣirūna bihā* (لا يبصرون بها): The signs of Allah in the universe.

*Lā yasma'ūna bihā* (لا يسمعون بها): The truth and what is good.

*Ka-l-an'ām* (كالأنعام): Like cattle, in failing to benefit from their hearts, eyes and ears.

*Al-ghāfilūn* (الغافلون): That is, heedless of the signs of Allah, of what they were created for, and of what is intended for them and through them.

*Wa-li-llāhi al-asmā' al-ḥusnā* (ولله الأسماء الحسنى): Al-asmā' is the plural of ism (name), and al-ḥusnā is the feminine of al-aḥsan (the most beautiful). The Most Beautiful Names belong to Allah exclusively, and none of His creatures shares them with Him.

*Wa-dharū* (وذروا): Leave, abandon.

*Yulḥidūn* (يلحدون): They incline them toward falsehood.

*Wa-mimman khalaqnā* (وممن خلقنا): That is, from among mankind.

**Meaning of the verses:**

Following the mention of guidance and misguidance, and that the one who is guided is the one Allah guides and the one who strays is the one Allah leads astray, Allah, exalted is He, informs us that He has created many of the jinn and humankind for Hell, knowing that they reject His guidance, act arrogantly toward His worship, and wage war against His prophets and messengers. Their rejection of guidance and their arrogance toward worship render their faculties inoperative: the heart does not comprehend what is said to it, the eye does not see what it looks upon, and the ear does not hear what it is informed of and told. Thus they become like cattle, indeed even more astray, because cattle have not departed from the path for which they were driven and created, whereas those have departed from the path they were commanded to follow and created for, namely the worship of Allah alone, without partner, so that they might be saved from punishment and attain bliss in the Abode of Delight. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those are the heedless﴾ affirms a reality: their persistence in misguidance was the result of their heedlessness of the cosmic signs of Allah, so that they do not reflect upon them and thereby know that the true deity is Allah alone and worship Him, and heedlessness of the revealed signs of Allah, so that they do not contemplate them and thereby know that Allah is the Manifest Truth and worship Him alone in accordance with what He has legislated for them in His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet. This is what the first verse [179] indicates.

As for the second verse in this context [180], which is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And to Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾: In it Allah informs us that the Most Beautiful Names belong to Him exclusively, and none of His creation shares them with Him. The Prophet ﷺ informed us that they are one hundred names less one, that is, ninety-nine names, and they occur dispersed throughout the noble Qur'an. Allah commanded His servants to call upon Him by them: "O Allah, O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful, O Lord, O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting," and that is when they ask Him and seek from Him what they cannot accomplish. He also commanded them to leave the people of deviation and misguidance who deviate concerning the names of Allah, by distorting them, or denying them, or likening them to creation. He commanded His believing servants to leave these people to Him, so that He may recompense them with just recompense for what they used to say and do, for their disputation is of no benefit to them, nor is it a source of glory for the believers or for them.

This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third [181], which is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And among those We have created is a community that guides by the truth and by it acts justly﴾: When He mentioned that He had created many of the jinn and humankind for Hell, He mentioned here that He had created another kind, from humankind and the jinn, for Paradise, and described their qualities by which they merit Paradise, just as He had described the qualities of the people of Hell by which they merited Hell. He said, ﴿And among those We have created﴾ from mankind, ﴿a community﴾ great in number, ﴿that guides﴾ themselves and others ﴿by the truth﴾, which is the guidance of Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and by it acts justly﴾ in their judgments and rulings, so that they are equitable and do not oppress. Among this community is every righteous person within the community of Islam who lives by the Book and the Sunnah in belief, speech, action, rule, judgment, conduct and character. May Allah make us among them and gather us in their company.

**Lessons from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the principle that happiness and misery were decreed by the pen of divine decree and destiny, so each is facilitated for what he was created for.

2. The descent of the human being to a lower depth than the depth of animals, which occurs when he disbelieves in his Lord, disables his faculties from benefiting from them, and confines his concern to the worldly life.

3. Clarification that calamity lies in heedlessness of the signs of Allah and turning away from them.

4. The command to call upon Allah by His Most Beautiful Names, such as "O Lord, O Most Gracious," "O Mighty, O Compeller."

5. The prohibition of interpreting the names and attributes of Allah in distorted ways, as the polytheists did with regard to Allah: al-Lat, derived from His name Allah, and al-'Uzza, derived from His name al-'Aziz, which they used to name their false deities. This is the deviation (ilḥād) for which Allah threatened its practitioners with recompense.

6. Those of Paradise who were created for it are those who guide by the Book and the Sunnah and judge by them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 182–186:

Explanation of the words:

*Kadhdhabu bi-ayatina* (they denied Our signs): that is, the signs of the Noble Qur'an.

*Sanastadrijuhum* (We will gradually draw them on): that is, We will lure them while they descend into the pit of punishment step by step, until they arrive at the punishment. This happens by pouring blessings upon them while they persist in denial and disobedience, until they reach the appointed term set for them, and then they are seized in one single seizing.

*Wa-umli lahum inna kaydi matin* (And I give them respite; indeed My plan is firm): that is, I give them time and do not hasten their punishment, until they reach it through their false deeds. This is the plan against them, and it is a firm, severe plan.

*Ma bi-sahibihim min jinnah* (there is no madness in their companion): their companion is Muhammad (ﷺ), and *jinnah* means madness; those spoken of are the disbelievers of Quraysh.

*Malakut as-samawat* (the dominion of the heavens): that is, the kingdom of the heavens, except that the word *malakut* is greater in meaning than the word *mulk* (kingdom).

*Fa-bi-ayyi hadithin ba'dahu* (then in what statement after it): that is, after the Mighty Qur'an.

*Wa-nadharuhum fi tughyanihim* (And We leave them in their transgression): that is, We leave them in their disbelief and wrongdoing.

*Ya'mahun* (wandering blindly): bewildered, hesitating, not knowing any way out or path to salvation.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted One informs that those who denied His signs, which He sent with His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), did not believe in them, and persisted in polytheism and error, turning away from monotheism and guidance. He informs that He will draw them on by seizing them little by little, step after step, until the punishment becomes due against them; then He sends it down upon them and they perish. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 187–188:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Sa'a (the Hour): the time at which worldly life ends in complete annihilation.

Ayyana mursaha: when its time of establishment (arrival) is.

La yujalliha li-waqtiha: none will reveal it at its appointed time except Him, glorified and exalted.

Baghtah: suddenly, without expectation or waiting.

Hafiyy 'anha: one who asks about it insistently and exaggeratedly, to the point that he comes to know its time of arrival.

Al-ghayb (the unseen): that which is hidden from our senses and our minds, so it is not perceived by any sense nor grasped by reason. Here it refers to what will happen in the near or distant future.

Al-su': everything that harms the servant in his soul or his body.

In ana illa nadhir: that is, I am nothing but a warner and a bearer of good news; I am not a god who manages affairs or knows the unseen.

The meaning of the verses:

There is no doubt that some individuals from Quraysh or others asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour, when it would occur. Allah, the Exalted, informed him of their question and taught him the answer, so He, Mighty and Majestic, said while addressing His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its appointed time to occur?﴾ That is, when is the time of its occurrence and establishment? Say to them: ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾, that is, the knowledge of the time of its establishment is with my Lord alone, ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾, that is, none will manifest it at its first appointed time except Him. ﴿It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the matter of its knowledge is weighty for the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. ﴿It will not come to you except suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly. Then He said to him: these ignorant people ask you about the Hour, ﴿as though you were insistent about it﴾, that is, as though you were insistent in questioning and exaggerating in seeking its knowledge until you came to know it. Say to them: ﴿Its knowledge is only with Allah﴾ exclusively, ﴿but most people do not know﴾. That is why they ask him, since its concealment serves lofty wisdoms; had people known it, they would not have asked, nor would they ask. Rather, ignorance is what has entangled them in such questions, and this is what the first verse [187] indicates.

As for the second verse [188], the Exalted commanded His Messenger to say to those who asked about the Hour, when its time of arrival is: ﴿I possess no power over my own benefit or harm﴾, neither good nor evil, ﴿except as Allah wills﴾ some of that, for He helps me to attract it or to repel it. So how then would I know the time of the Hour's arrival so that you ask me about it? ﴿And if I knew the unseen﴾ as you suppose, ﴿I would have acquired abundance of good, and no harm would have touched me.﴾ That is because if I knew when there would be fertility and when drought, when high prices and when plenty, I could easily acquire much good when it exists, and guard against and repel evil before it occurs. O people, I am only a warner of the consequences of polytheism and sins, and a bearer of good news of the results of faith, monotheism and righteous deeds. I am not a god who knows the unseen. And this duty of mine, clearly, is giving good news and warning, from which only believers benefit. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿I am only a warner and a bearer of good news to a people who believe.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- The knowledge of the Hour returns to Allah alone; whoever is asked about it other than Allah is not more knowledgeable than the questioner.

2- The Hour has signs, some of which are in the Book and some in the Sunnah. This does not mean that they specify its time; they are only preliminary indications that show its nearness.

3- Allah has exclusive knowledge of the unseen, so none knows the unseen except Allah. Whoever Allah has taught some of it knows it, as He taught His Prophet ﷺ some of the hidden matters. One who has been taught something is not described as knowing the unseen; rather it is said that his Lord taught him the unseen of such and such, and so he knew it.

4- If the Messenger does not possess benefit or harm for himself, how can it be asked of him? And if the Messenger does not possess it, does anyone other than him among the servants possess it? Once you understand this, the misguidance of people becomes clear to you, those who call upon the dead, asking and supplicating at their graves, and who claim that they do not call upon them but merely seek intercession through them.

So how then would I know the time of the Hour's arrival so that you ask me about it? ﴿And if I knew the unseen﴾ as you suppose, ﴿I would have acquired abundance of good, and no harm would have touched me.﴾ That is because if I knew when there would be fertility and when drought, when high prices and when plenty, I could easily acquire much good when it exists, and guard against and repel evil before it occurs. O people, I am only a warner of the consequences of polytheism and sins, and a bearer of good news of the results of faith, monotheism and righteous deeds. I am not a god who knows the unseen. And this duty of mine, clearly, is giving good news and warning, from which only believers benefit. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿I am only a warner and a bearer of good news to a people who believe.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- The knowledge of the Hour returns to Allah alone; whoever is asked about it other than Allah is not more knowledgeable than the questioner.

2- The Hour has signs, some of which are in the Book and some in the Sunnah. This does not mean that they specify its time; they are only preliminary indications that show its nearness.

3- Allah has exclusive knowledge of the unseen, so none knows the unseen except Allah. Whoever Allah has taught some of it knows it, as He taught His Prophet ﷺ some of the hidden matters. One who has been taught something is not described as knowing the unseen; rather it is said that his Lord taught him the unseen of such and such, and so he knew it.

4- If the Messenger does not possess benefit or harm for himself, how can it be asked of him? And if the Messenger does not possess it, does anyone other than him among the servants possess it? Once you understand this, the misguidance of people becomes clear to you, those who call upon the dead, asking and supplicating at their graves, and who claim that they do not call upon them but merely seek intercession through them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 189–193:

Explanation of the words:

*min nafsin wahidah* (from a single soul): this is the soul of Adam, peace be upon him.

*wa-ja'ala minha zawjaha* (and made from it its mate): i.e., He created from it its mate, who is Eve (Hawwa'). She was created from the left rib of Adam.

*li-yaskuna ilayha* (that he might find rest in her): i.e., that he might become familiar with her and feel at ease with her, because she is of his own kind.

*falamma taghashshaha* (when he covered her): i.e., had intercourse with her.

*famarrat bihi* (then she went about with it): i.e., she went and came, attending to her needs, because the pregnancy was light in the first months.

*falamma athqalat* (when she became heavy): i.e., the pregnancy became heavy in her womb.

*la-in ataytana salihan* (if You give us a righteous child): i.e., a righteous child, not an animal but a human being.

*ja'ala lahu shuraka'* (they made for Him associates): i.e., they named him ʿAbd al-Harith, whereas his true name is ʿAbd Allah, may His majesty be exalted.

*fa-ta'ala Allahu ʿamma yushrikun* (Exalted is God above what they associate): i.e., the people of Mecca, who associated idols with the worship of God.

*wa-in tadʿuhum ila al-huda* (and if you call them to guidance): i.e., the idols will not follow you.

Meaning of the verses:

Almighty God says to those who asked about the Hour out of obstinacy and arrogance from among the people of polytheism: He, that is God, *"who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate"*, is the God who deserves to be worshipped, not the idols and images.
