His saying *"that he might find rest in her"* gives the reason for creating her mate from him, for had she been of another kind, familiarity and intimacy would not have arisen between them. His saying *"when he covered her"* means for intercourse, and he had intercourse with her, *"she bore a light burden and went about with it"* because it was light. *"When she became heavy"* means the burden made her heavy. *"They called upon God"*, that is Adam and Eve, called upon their Lord, the Exalted, meaning they asked Him, saying *"If You give us a righteous child"*, i.e., a righteous boy, *"we shall surely be among the thankful"*, i.e., to You. The Lord, the Exalted, answered them and gave them a righteous child. His saying, *"But when He gave them a righteous child, they made for Him associates in what He had given them"*: Eve named him ʿAbd al-Harith by the deception of Iblis, who suggested this name to them. It is among the hidden shirk that is pardoned, like saying "Had it not been for the doctor, so-and-so would have died." His saying *"Exalted is God above what they associate"* refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh who associated their idols and images with the worship of God, as evidenced by His saying afterward, *"Do they associate what creates nothing, while they are themselves created?"*, i.e., of the created beings. *"And they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves,"* when they are asked to do so, *"because they are lifeless objects with no life or power."* His saying *"And if you call them to guidance"*, i.e., if you call those idols, *"to guidance"*, when they have lost the way, *"they will not follow you,"* because they cannot distinguish right guidance from error. Therefore, *"it is all the same for you whether you call them or remain silent"*, i.e., you do not call them, for they will not follow you. Given that this is their state and this is their reality, is it right that such a being be worshipped, offered sacrifices, sworn by, attended at, called upon and sought for help? God forbid, but the polytheists do not understand.

1. Clarification of the origin of humankind: Adam and Eve, peace be upon them.

2. Clarification of the wisdom in the mate being of the same kind as the spouse, namely familiarity, intimacy and cooperation.

3. Clarification of the deception and misguidance of man by Iblis, who made the naming of their child ʿAbd al-Harith, which is ʿAbd Allah, appealing to Eve.

4. Shirk in naming is hidden shirk that is pardoned, and leaving it is better.

5. Condemnation of shirk and the polytheists, and clarification of the ignorance and folly of the polytheists, who worship what neither hears, sees, answers nor follows.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 194–198:

Explanation of the words:

ʿIbād amthālukum (عباد أمثالكم): that is, they are owned creatures, made like you, belonging to one Owner, who is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

Shurakāʾakum (شركاءكم): your idols, which you associate with Allah.

Thumma kīdūn (ثم كيدون): plot against me with whatever kinds of scheming you are able to.

Fa-lā tunẓirūn (فلا تنظرون): that is, do not give me respite, for I do not care about you.

Inna waliyyiya Allāh (إن وليي الله): that is, the One who manages my affairs, protects me and supports me is Allah, who sent down the Qur'an.

Wa-tarāhum yanẓurūn (وتراهم ينظرون): that is, you see the idols carved in the shape of men looking at you, while they do not see.

Meaning of the verses:

These five verses, in the context of what precedes them, came to establish the principle of monotheism (tawhid), to confirm it, to denounce association of partners with Allah (shirk), and to make it abhorrent, along with its adherents. The words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, those you invoke﴾, meaning worship-invocation, O polytheists, ﴿are servants like you﴾, meaning owned by Allah; Allah is their Owner just as you are owned by Allah and nurtured by Him. So how is it valid for you to worship them, when they are owned creatures like you, who possess for you neither benefit nor harm, nor for themselves? And if you doubt the soundness of this, then call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful in your claim that they are gods deserving of worship. Indeed, if you were to call upon them, they would not respond. And how could they respond, when they are inanimate and have no life? ﴿Do they have feet with which they walk, or do they have hands with which they strike, or do they have eyes with which they see, or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾ There is none of that for them, so how then could they respond, and by what right are they worshipped, invoked, and hoped in, when they are utterly devoid of any trace of power and life?

Then Allah commanded His Messenger to declare to them that he does not fear them and does not reckon anything of them, if they worship them and fear them. So He said to him: Say to these polytheists, ﴿Call your partners, then plot against me﴾, you and they together, ﴿and do not give me respite﴾, meaning do not delay me for an hour. That is because ﴿my guardian is Allah, who sent down the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and He is the Protector of the righteous﴾. So He supports me against you and shields me from your scheming; indeed He is the Protector and Guardian of the believers. As for you, ﴿and those you invoke besides Him﴾, meaning besides Allah, these idols, ﴿cannot help you nor help themselves﴾. And there is another matter: ﴿if you call them to guidance, they do not hear﴾, let alone if you call them to misguidance. So how is it valid to worship one who does not answer his caller, neither in ease nor in hardship?

Finally, the Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And you see them﴾, meaning you see those deities, which are statues of stone, ﴿looking at you﴾ when you face them, because their eyes are always open, while in fact ﴿they do not see﴾. Do images and statues see?

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the proof against the polytheists by unveiling the reality of what they claim to be gods; then they turn out to be idols that neither hear nor respond, having no hands, no feet, no ears, and no eyes.

2- The obligation to rely upon Allah, to expel fear from the soul, and to stand against falsehood and its people with courage, patience, and steadfastness, relying on Allah and His guardianship, for He protects the righteous.

3- The permissibility of exaggerating in repelling people from falsehood and evil by mentioning their defects and deficiencies.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 7, verses 199–202:

Explanation of the words:

Al-'afw (forgiveness, pardon): that which is easy and entails no hardship, that which comes without strain.

Bil-'urf (with what is known): i.e., what is known in the Shari'ah as something commanded or recommended.

Wa-a'rid 'ani al-jahilin (and turn away from the ignorant): the ignorant (al-jahilun) are those whose hearts have not been illumined by the light of knowledge and piety. Turning away from them means not holding them to account for their evil speech or deeds.

Nazgh al-shaytan (a prick of Satan): i.e., his whispering of evil.

Fa-sta'idh billah (then seek refuge in Allah): i.e., say "I seek refuge in Allah," which will repel it from you; He is indeed All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Ittaqu (those who fear Allah): i.e., shirk and sins.

Ta'if min al-shaytan (a visitation from Satan): i.e., something of his whispering has touched them.

Wa-ikhwanuhum yamudduunahum fi al-ghayy (and their brothers push them further into error): i.e., the brothers of the devils, from among the people of shirk and sins, push them further into error.

Thumma la yuqsirun (then they do not hold back): i.e., they do not refrain from error, which is misguidance, evil and corruption.

The meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted taught His Messenger how to argue with the polytheists to refute their falsehood in worshipping other than Allah and associating partners with Him, He taught him in this verse the most lofty of manners and the most excellent and complete of morals. He said to him: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is known as good, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, meaning: take from people's characters what is easy for them to bear and what is facilitated for them to do; do not demand of them what they do not possess or what they do not know; enjoin upon them what is good; and turn away from the ignorant among them, so do not rebuke them or speak harshly to them. The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked by Jibril (peace be upon him) about the meaning of this verse, and he said: (You pardon the one who wronged you, you maintain ties with the one who cut you off, and you give to the one who withheld from you).

As for His words ﴿And if a prick from Satan should afflict you﴾, meaning: it stirs up your anger so that you do not adhere to this manner you were commanded with, ﴿then seek refuge in Allah﴾ to repel it from you; indeed He is All-Hearing of your words, All-Knowing of your conditions.

Then the Exalted said, establishing the ruling of seeking refuge and clarifying its benefit for whoever takes hold of it: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾, meaning: fear their Lord, so they do not associate anything with Him, do not neglect the obligations, and do not approach the prohibitions. ﴿When a visitation from Satan touches them﴾, by his prodding them with the stirring of anger or desire, ﴿they remember, and behold, they see clearly﴾, seeing the ugliness of sin and the evil outcome of its doer, so they refrain from it and do not commit it.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And their brothers﴾, meaning: the brothers of the devils from among the people of shirk and sins, ﴿push them further﴾, meaning: the devils, ﴿into error﴾, meaning: into sins and misguidance, and they increase them by adorning these for them and driving them to them, ﴿then they do not hold back﴾ from committing them, nor do they refrain from perpetrating them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The command to adhere to good manners and to adorn oneself with the most complete character, the highest of which is pardoning the one who wronged you, giving to the one who withheld from you, and maintaining ties with the one who cut you off.

2- The obligation to seek refuge in Allah upon feeling whispering, anger, or the adorning of falsehood.

3- The virtue of taqwa, which is performing the obligations and abandoning the prohibitions.

4- The evil of being the brother of devils, for the one who has them is not restrained from error, which is evil and corruption, by their pushing him on.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked by Jibril (peace be upon him) about the meaning of this verse, and he said: (You pardon the one who wronged you, you maintain ties with the one who cut you off, and you give to the one who withheld from you).

As for His words ﴿And if a prick from Satan should afflict you﴾, meaning: it stirs up your anger so that you do not adhere to this manner you were commanded with, ﴿then seek refuge in Allah﴾ to repel it from you; indeed He is All-Hearing of your words, All-Knowing of your conditions.

Then the Exalted said, establishing the ruling of seeking refuge and clarifying its benefit for whoever takes hold of it: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah﴾, meaning: fear their Lord, so they do not associate anything with Him, do not neglect the obligations, and do not approach the prohibitions. ﴿When a visitation from Satan touches them﴾, by his prodding them with the stirring of anger or desire, ﴿they remember, and behold, they see clearly﴾, seeing the ugliness of sin and the evil outcome of its doer, so they refrain from it and do not commit it.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿And their brothers﴾, meaning: the brothers of the devils from among the people of shirk and sins, ﴿push them further﴾, meaning: the devils, ﴿into error﴾, meaning: into sins and misguidance, and they increase them by adorning these for them and driving them to them, ﴿then they do not hold back﴾ from committing them, nor do they refrain from perpetrating them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The command to adhere to good manners and to adorn oneself with the most complete character, the highest of which is pardoning the one who wronged you, giving to the one who withheld from you, and maintaining ties with the one who cut you off.

2- The obligation to seek refuge in Allah upon feeling whispering, anger, or the adorning of falsehood.

3- The virtue of taqwa, which is performing the obligations and abandoning the prohibitions.

4- The evil of being the brother of devils, for the one who has them is not restrained from error, which is evil and corruption, by their pushing him on.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 7, verses 203–206:

Explanation of the words:

*Qalu lawla ijtabaytaha* (﴿قالوا لولا اجتبيتها﴾): That is, you invented it and fabricated it from yourself and brought it to us.

*Hadha basa'ira min rabbikum* (﴿هذا بصائر من ربكم﴾): That is, this Qur'an is proofs, evidences and arguments for what you have brought and what I call you to. It is therefore a stronger proof than the sign you are demanding.

*Fastami'u lahu wa-ansitu* (﴿فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا﴾): That is, seek to hear it and make an effort to listen, and be silent at that time, that is, keep quiet so that you hear in a way that benefits you.

*Wa-khifatan* (﴿وخيفة﴾): That is, out of fear.

*Bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal* (﴿بالغدو والآصال﴾): *al-ghuduw* is the beginning of the day, and *al-asal* is its end.

*Min al-ghafilin* (﴿من الغافلين﴾): That is, heedless of the remembrance of God, the Exalted.

*Inna alladhina 'inda rabbika* (﴿إن الذين عند ربك﴾): That is, the angels.

*Yusabbihunahu* (﴿يسبحونه﴾): They glorify Him with their tongues, by saying such things as "Glory be to God and praise be to Him."

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the instruction given to the Messenger ﷺ on how to respond to the polytheists, his opponents. God the Exalted says concerning the polytheists of Makkah: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign,﴾ O our Messenger, ﴿as they request, they say,﴾ to you, ﴿"Why have you not invented it?"﴾ That is, why did you not create and originate it from yourself, since your Lord has not given it? Say to them: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord.﴾ I am a servant of God and His messenger, and I do not fabricate against Him. ﴿This is insights from your Lord﴾: this Qur'an that is revealed to me consists of proofs and arguments for the truth of my claim, for establishing my message, and for the soundness of what I call you to: faith, monotheism, and abandoning polytheism and sins. So why do you not believe and follow? Do you believe in a single sign and not believe in many signs? Where do your minds go? In connection with the explanation of the proofs and lights of the Qur'an, God the Exalted commanded His believing servants that when the Qur'an is recited to them, they should listen and be silent, whether it is the Friday sermon from the pulpit or at other times. God the Exalted says: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent,﴾ that is, make an effort to listen and intend it, ﴿that you may receive mercy,﴾ by refraining from speech. That is, in hope that the mercy of the Qur'an's guidance will reach you, so that you are guided and receive mercy, because the Qur'an is guidance and mercy for the believers.

Then God the Exalted commanded His Messenger, and his community, which follows him in this perfection, saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself,﴾ that is, secretly, ﴿humbly,﴾ that is, with submission and humility, ﴿and fearfully,﴾ that is, with fear and awe, ﴿and without loudness of speech﴾, which is secrecy, by making oneself alone hear it or those beside him only. His saying ﴿in the mornings and evenings﴾ means at the beginnings and ends of the day. He forbade him from neglecting the remembrance, which is heedlessness, saying: ﴿And do not be among the heedless.﴾ He mentioned to him the glorification and worship of the angels so that he might emulate them, continuing in worship and remembrance night and day, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord﴾, who are the angels in the highest realm, ﴿do not disdain from His worship﴾, that is, from His obedience in what He has commanded them and assigned them to, ﴿and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.﴾ So emulate them and do not be among the heedless.

Lessons from the verses:

1. The Qur'an is the greatest sign; indeed, it is greater than all the signs given to the messengers, peace be upon them.

2. The obligation to be silent when the Qur'an is recited, especially in the Friday sermon from the pulpit, and during the imam's loud recitation in prayer.

3. The obligation to remember God in the mornings and evenings.

4. Explanation of the etiquette of remembrance, which is:
   1. Secrecy.
   2. Humility and submission.
   3. Fear and awe.
   4. Keeping it private and not raising the voice in it, unlike what the Sufis do.

5. The legitimacy of emulating the righteous and following them in doing good and abandoning wrongdoing.

6. The prescription of prostration at His saying ﴿and to Him they prostrate﴾. This is the first prostration of the Qur'an. The reciter and the listener prostrate; as for the listener, there is no prostration upon him. One faces the qibla for it, says "Allahu Akbar" when prostrating and when rising from it, and does not give the salam. Being in a state of ablution is better.
